metadata.title: Product Streams
metadata.description: Outcome-based product streams for the Paramedical and Mental Health Practice Platform domain, modeled on Health Cloud Initiative (HCI): the paramedical practice journeys from a booked slot through the electronic patient record, outcome measurement and a paid Vecozo declaration to management insight; the mental health care (GGZ) journeys of zorgprestatiemodel treatment coordination and blended e-health care; the patient and network journeys through Uw Zorg Online, Quli personal health environments, ZorgDomein and ZorgMail and practice websites; and the platform journeys of partner integration, label consolidation into HCI One and NEN 7510 / ISO 27001 compliance that keep 40,000+ professionals and 4 million+ patients served every day.

definitions.productBrick: A reusable implementation-facing building block used to realize one or more product streams.
definitions.productStream: A high-level, outcome-based experience that delivers customer or business value.

metadata.flowModelNote: Each stream carries only stream-specific flows, names the supporting bricks used in each step and the persona acting in it, and lists the external systems (Vecozo, insurers and municipalities, ZorgDomein and ZorgMail, HIS/AIS and hospital information systems, the LDF and Keurmerk registers, MedMij data sources, Mollie, Twinfield, exercise-app partners, the app stores, DigiD and UZI, and certification bodies) the flow depends on.

rootGroups.name: Paramedical Practice Journeys
rootGroups.description: From a referral or a patient request to a booked slot, from intake to a closed episode in a guideline-compliant dossier, from a measurement instrument to an outcome delivered to the LDF, from a registered treatment to a paid GDS801 declaration through Vecozo, and from registrations to management decisions: the journeys that give physiotherapists and allied health therapists back the working day per week they report losing to administration.

streams.name: Schedule Appointments and Online Booking
streams.description: Take a paramedical practice from a referral, a phone call or a patient request to a booked and confirmed slot in the agenda that FysioRoadmap calls the central heart of the practice. The stream covers the multi-therapist, multi-location agenda, 24/7 online booking from the practice website and the Uw Zorg Online app synchronised with that agenda, waiting-list handling, reminders that cut no-shows, group lessons and subscriptions in SpotOnMedics style, and the mobile agenda in the Zorgverlener App. Because invoices and declarations are generated from the agenda, every booking must already carry the patient, the therapist, the location and the treatment code that the declaration later needs.
outcomes: A patient who finds the practice on the website or in the app books a first appointment without a phone call, and the slot appears in the therapist's agenda with the right treatment code
Therapists across locations see one agenda on desktop and mobile and no longer double-book rooms, equipment or group lessons
Reminders and the waiting list keep the agenda full, so cancellations are refilled and no-shows fall
Every agenda entry is complete enough to generate the invoice or GDS801 declaration without later correction

flows.title: From Online Request to Confirmed First Appointment
flows.description: A new patient with a shoulder complaint books a first physiotherapy appointment through the practice website or the Uw Zorg Online app, the practice checks the request against the agenda and the intake requirements, and the slot is confirmed and reminded until the patient walks in.
flows.trigger: A patient opens the online booking page of the practice website or taps 'book an appointment' in the Uw Zorg Online app, with or without a GP referral.
flows.successSignal: The first appointment is confirmed in the agenda with therapist, location, room and a provisional treatment code, the patient has received a confirmation and a reminder, and the intake questionnaire link has been sent.

steps.title: Open online booking from the practice website or the patient app
keyFacts: The practice website shows a booking entry point that reads the live availability of every therapist and location from the agenda; SpotOnMedics-style 24/7 online booking means a patient can book on Sunday evening for Monday morning.
Patients who already use the Uw Zorg Online app for their GP see the physiotherapy practice as another care provider and book in the same app without a new account.

The booking page asks for complaint type, preferred location and whether the patient has a referral; in the Netherlands physiotherapy is directly accessible (DTF), so a referral is optional for most complaints.
painPoints: Practices that publish a static contact form instead of live booking keep answering the phone for every first appointment.
Patients do not know which therapist or specialisation (manual therapy, pelvic physiotherapy, paediatric physiotherapy) fits their complaint and book the wrong slot.

dependencies.description: Booking entry point on the website.

steps.title: Match the request to a therapist, location and slot
keyFacts: The agenda holds per-therapist working hours, per-location rooms and equipment, treatment durations per appointment type and specialisation cards so that a pelvic-physiotherapy request only shows pelvic-physiotherapy slots.
Practices with 2 to 15 therapists on several locations run one shared agenda, and the practice owner decides which slots are bookable online and which are held back for follow-ups.
painPoints: When online-bookable slots are not fenced, new patients fill the follow-up capacity and existing patients cannot continue their treatment series.
Multi-location practices without room and equipment resources double-book the shockwave device or the exercise room.

dependencies.name: Online Booking, Waiting List and Reminders

steps.title: Identify or create the patient and check for an existing dossier
keyFacts: A booking from the app arrives with a verified identity; a booking from the website is matched on name, date of birth and e-mail against existing patients so that a returning patient is not created twice.
The booking creates the patient and a provisional episode in the dossier so that the therapist opens the first appointment with an intake ready to fill.
painPoints: Duplicate patients created from website bookings split the treatment history and later cause declaration rejections on the wrong BSN.
Practices that collect the BSN and insurance details by phone after the booking lose the first appointment to administration.

dependencies.name: Identity, Access and Strong Authentication (UZI/DigiD)
dependencies.how: Supplies the verified identity for bookings that come through the patient app.

steps.title: Confirm the slot and send the intake questionnaire
keyFacts: The confirmation carries date, time, location, therapist and what to bring (identification, insurance card, referral letter if any) and includes the link to the digital intake so that the therapist reads the complaint history before the patient arrives.
Confirmations go to the app inbox when the patient uses Uw Zorg Online and by e-mail or SMS otherwise.
painPoints: Patients who fill the intake on paper in the waiting room delay the first consult and the therapist retypes the answers into the dossier.

dependencies.name: Online Booking, Waiting List and Reminders
dependencies.how: Sends the confirmation with the intake link through app, e-mail or SMS.

dependencies.name: Patient App and Web Portal
dependencies.how: Shows the confirmation and the intake questionnaire in the patient app.

steps.title: Remind the patient and handle reschedules and cancellations
keyFacts: Reminders go out at a practice-configured interval before the appointment; the patient can reschedule or cancel from the reminder within the practice's cancellation window, and a freed slot is offered to the waiting list.
Late cancellations and no-shows are recorded on the appointment so that the practice can apply its no-show tariff (not declarable to the insurer) through a patient invoice.
painPoints: Patients who cancel by voicemail outside opening hours leave a slot empty that a waiting-list patient would have taken.
Practices that do not record no-shows consistently cannot invoice them and cannot see which therapists or slots attract them.

dependencies.name: Agenda and Multi-location Scheduling
dependencies.how: Records reschedules, cancellations and no-shows on the agenda entry.

dependencies.name: Patient Appointment Self-service
dependencies.how: Lets the patient reschedule or cancel from the app within the practice rules.

steps.title: See the day on desktop and in the Zorgverlener App
keyFacts: Therapists who work at several locations or on home visits open the day in the Zorgverlener App, see who is next, whether the intake was filled and where the appointment is, and mark arrival or no-show from the phone.
The agenda entry already carries the treatment code, so at the end of the day the declaration engine can generate the claims from the agenda without extra registration.
painPoints: Therapists who cannot see the agenda on the phone during home visits call the front desk for every change.

dependencies.name: Agenda and Multi-location Scheduling
dependencies.how: Keeps the desktop and mobile day view in sync across locations.

flows.title: Run Group Lessons, Programmes and Subscriptions
flows.description: A practice sets up group lessons (medical fitness, fall prevention, COPD or back-school groups), lets patients subscribe to a programme or a monthly membership, plans the sessions in the agenda with room and trainer capacity, and tracks attendance so that programmes are invoiced to the patient or declared to the insurer correctly.
flows.trigger: The practice owner decides to offer a group programme or a patient asks to join an existing group after individual treatment.
flows.successSignal: The group runs with the planned capacity, every participant has a subscription or programme record, attendance is registered per session and the invoicing or declaration follows the right route.

steps.title: Define the group programme, its schedule and capacity
keyFacts: A group programme has a name, a trainer, a room with a maximum number of participants, a session schedule (for example twice a week for twelve weeks) and a pricing model: a patient-paid subscription, a fixed-price programme, or a declarable group treatment such as supervised exercise therapy for COPD or claudication.
SpotOnMedics-style group management shows occupancy per session so that the owner can open a second group when a waiting list forms.
painPoints: Groups planned in a spreadsheet next to the agenda collide with individual appointments in the same room.

dependencies.name: Group Lessons, Programmes and Subscriptions
dependencies.how: Defines the programme, pricing model, schedule and capacity.

dependencies.name: Agenda and Multi-location Scheduling
dependencies.how: Reserves the room and the trainer's time for every session in the schedule.

steps.title: Enrol participants and start their subscriptions
keyFacts: Existing patients are enrolled from their dossier so that the group participation is part of the treatment history; new members of a fitness subscription are created as patients with a subscription and no clinical episode.
Patients can enrol online from the website or the app when the owner opens a programme for self-service enrolment.
painPoints: Practices that manage memberships in a separate fitness system reconcile two member lists every month.
Participants whose supervised programme is declarable are enrolled as subscription members by mistake and the insurer claim is never generated.

dependencies.name: Group Lessons, Programmes and Subscriptions
dependencies.how: Enrols the participant and starts the subscription or programme record with its pricing route.

dependencies.name: Patient Dossier and Care Pathways
dependencies.how: Links the participation to the patient record and the clinical episode when there is one.

dependencies.name: Online Booking, Waiting List and Reminders
dependencies.how: Lets patients enrol in an open programme from the website or app.

steps.title: Plan the sessions and register attendance
keyFacts: Each session is an agenda entry with the participant list; the trainer ticks attendance on the tablet or in the Zorgverlener App at the start of the session.
Attendance feeds both the declarable group treatment (one registration per participant per session) and the subscription (sessions used of the entitlement).
painPoints: Attendance ticked on a paper list is typed in days later, and declarations for absent participants slip through.

dependencies.name: Agenda and Multi-location Scheduling
dependencies.how: Holds each session as an agenda entry with its participant list.

dependencies.name: Zorgverlener Mobile App
dependencies.how: Lets the trainer register attendance per participant from the mobile app.

dependencies.name: Group Lessons, Programmes and Subscriptions
dependencies.how: Stores attendance against the programme or subscription.

steps.title: Handle waiting lists, absences and substitutions
keyFacts: Participants who cannot attend can book a catch-up session in another group within the same programme; a full group keeps a waiting list that is offered a place when a participant stops.
Trainer absence triggers a substitution or a rescheduled session with notifications to all participants.
painPoints: Cancelling a session by calling twelve participants one by one is the reason many practices keep groups small.

dependencies.name: Online Booking, Waiting List and Reminders
dependencies.how: Notifies participants of changes and offers freed places to the waiting list.

dependencies.name: Group Lessons, Programmes and Subscriptions
dependencies.how: Applies the programme rules for catch-up sessions and substitutions.

steps.title: Close the period and route the charges to invoice or declaration
keyFacts: At period end the subscription fee is invoiced to the member, the fixed-price programme is invoiced on enrolment or in instalments, and the declarable group sessions are handed to the declaration flow with the group-treatment code per participant.
The owner sees occupancy, attendance rate and revenue per programme to decide which groups to continue.
painPoints: Practices that invoice subscriptions manually forget price changes and chase members who stopped months ago.

dependencies.name: Group Lessons, Programmes and Subscriptions
dependencies.how: Produces the subscription and programme charges and the declarable session registrations.

dependencies.name: Patient Dossier and Care Pathways
dependencies.how: Records the group sessions in the episode so that the declaration engine can pick them up.

streams.name: Keep the Electronic Patient Record
streams.description: Take a treatment episode from intake to a closed dossier that passes an insurer audit and a KNGF, NVLF or NVD guideline check with as little typing as possible. The stream covers discipline-specific care pathways and guideline templates, the clinical reasoning and treatment plan, session notes with voice-to-text and AI summaries, documents and correspondence, measurement moments in the pathway, and the dossier audit rules that check completeness before the episode is declared or closed. It exists because physiotherapists report about a full working day per week on administration and because the dossier is the evidence behind every declaration, every quality-register delivery and every report to a referrer.
outcomes: A therapist documents the intake, the treatment plan and every session inside the consult time, with voice-to-text and templates instead of free typing
Every episode follows the care pathway of its discipline and guideline, so audit rules find nothing missing when the episode is declared or closed
Correspondence with the referrer and the patient is generated from the dossier instead of written twice
Records are complete, traceable and retained under the AVG and the WGBO retention duty

flows.title: From Intake to a Guideline-based Treatment Plan
flows.description: A physiotherapist opens the first appointment with a new patient, records the anamnesis and examination in the discipline template, applies the care pathway that fits the diagnosis (for example a KNGF guideline for low back pain), sets goals with the patient and starts the treatment plan that every later session refers to.
flows.trigger: The first appointment of a new episode starts, with a digital intake already filled by the patient or an empty dossier when the patient walked in.
flows.successSignal: The episode carries a coded diagnosis, a chosen care pathway with planned measurement moments, patient goals and a treatment plan, and the referrer has received an intake report where a referral exists.

steps.title: Open the episode with the digital intake and referral
keyFacts: The intake questionnaire the patient filled at booking, the referral letter received through ZorgDomein and the insurance details already sit in the episode when the therapist opens the appointment from the agenda.

For directly accessible physiotherapy the screening (DTF screening) is documented as the first step of the pathway; with a referral the referral date and referrer are recorded because the declaration and the report back depend on them.
painPoints: Referral letters that arrive as a PDF by e-mail are scanned and attached by hand, and the referral date is typed wrongly into the episode.
Therapists who cannot see the intake answers before the consult ask the same questions again.

dependencies.name: Patient Dossier and Care Pathways
dependencies.how: Opens the episode with the intake answers, referral data and insurance details in place.

dependencies.name: Referral and Secure Messaging Hub (ZorgDomein, ZorgMail)
dependencies.how: Delivers the ZorgDomein referral into the episode with referrer and referral date.

dependencies.name: Agenda and Multi-location Scheduling
dependencies.how: Opens the dossier from the agenda entry of the first appointment.

steps.title: Record the anamnesis and examination in the discipline template
keyFacts: The template follows the clinical reasoning of the discipline (for physiotherapy the KNGF directive on record keeping) with structured fields for complaint, history, expectations, examination findings and red flags, so that the record is complete for an audit without narrative padding.

Speech therapists, dietitians, occupational and exercise therapists get their own templates and terminology; the multidisciplinary HCI One platform keeps them per discipline rather than forcing one physiotherapy form on everyone.
painPoints: Generic free-text dossiers pass the therapist's own standard but fail the insurer's record audit on missing mandatory items.

dependencies.name: Clinical Guidelines and Discipline Templates
dependencies.how: Provides the structured intake and examination template of the discipline and guideline.

dependencies.name: Patient Dossier and Care Pathways
dependencies.how: Stores the structured intake in the episode.

steps.title: Dictate the findings with voice-to-text and review the AI draft
keyFacts: The therapist dictates the examination findings during or right after the consult; the draft is mapped to the template fields and shown for correction before it is saved, and the audit log records that a machine draft was reviewed.
SmartAI voice-to-text in CRS and the HCI One documentation assistant are positioned to reduce the administration time that therapists report, not to write the record unattended.
painPoints: Drafts that are saved without review put transcription errors about laterality or medication in a legal medical record.
Dictation in a shared treatment room is audible to the next patient.

dependencies.name: Voice-to-Text and AI Documentation
dependencies.how: Transcribes the dictation and proposes a structured draft for review.

dependencies.name: Audit Log, Consent and Information Security
dependencies.how: Logs that the draft was reviewed and by whom before it became part of the record.

steps.title: Choose the care pathway, code the diagnosis and plan the measurement moments
keyFacts: The care pathway for the diagnosis prescribes the measurement instruments and the moments (start, interim, end) at which PROMs are offered, so that the LDF delivery and the outcome dashboard receive complete series without the therapist remembering.
The diagnosis code and the indication (for example chronic list conditions that are reimbursed from the basic insurance after the first sessions) determine the declaration route later on.
painPoints: Episodes without a pathway miss the end measurement, and the practice's outcome data is incomplete in the benchmark.

dependencies.name: Clinical Guidelines and Discipline Templates
dependencies.how: Applies the pathway with its steps and measurement moments to the episode.

dependencies.name: Measurement Instruments and PROMs
dependencies.how: Schedules the PROMs and clinical measurements that the pathway prescribes.

dependencies.name: Patient Dossier and Care Pathways
dependencies.how: Records the diagnosis code and indication on the episode.

steps.title: Set goals with the patient and write the treatment plan
keyFacts: Goals are recorded in the patient's words next to the measurable targets (for example a PSK score), and the plan lists the expected number of sessions, the interventions and the home exercises.
The plan is visible to the patient in the app so that the patient sees what was agreed and what to do at home.
painPoints: Plans written as a single sentence give the insurer no basis to judge the number of sessions when the episode is audited.

dependencies.name: Patient Dossier and Care Pathways
dependencies.how: Stores goals, interventions and the expected number of sessions in the episode.

dependencies.name: Clinical Guidelines and Discipline Templates
dependencies.how: Provides the guideline-based plan structure for the diagnosis.

steps.title: Send the intake report to the referrer
keyFacts: Where a GP or specialist referred the patient, the intake report is generated from the recorded findings and plan and sent through ZorgMail or ZorgDomein so that the referrer's HIS files it in the patient's record.
The report is stored as correspondence in the episode with the sending date, which the audit rules check for referred episodes.
painPoints: Reports written as a separate letter duplicate the dossier text and are often skipped when the practice is busy.

dependencies.name: Referral and Secure Messaging Hub (ZorgDomein, ZorgMail)
dependencies.how: Sends the intake report to the referrer through ZorgMail or ZorgDomein.

dependencies.name: Patient Dossier and Care Pathways
dependencies.how: Generates the report from the dossier and files it as correspondence.

flows.title: From Session Notes to a Closed and Audited Episode
flows.description: Every treatment session is documented against the plan, interim measurements are recorded at the planned moments, the episode is checked by the dossier audit rules before declaration, and at the end the therapist closes the episode with an end evaluation and a report to the referrer, ready for retention and for quality-register delivery.
flows.trigger: A follow-up appointment starts, or the therapist decides with the patient that the treatment goals are reached or that treatment stops.
flows.successSignal: All sessions are documented, the audit rules report no missing items, the end measurement and evaluation are recorded, the end report is sent, and the episode is closed with its declarations released.

steps.title: Document the session against the treatment plan
keyFacts: The session note starts from the plan: which interventions were done, what changed, whether the home exercises were followed, and the next step; a SOEP-style note (subjective, objective, evaluation, plan) is the default in the physiotherapy template.
The note is tied to the agenda entry of the session, so a session without a note is visible to the practice owner and to the audit rules.
On home visits the therapist writes or dictates the note in the Zorgverlener App.
painPoints: Copy-pasted session notes ('same as last time') are the most common finding in insurer record audits.
Notes written at the end of the day after ten patients lose the details of each consult.

dependencies.name: Patient Dossier and Care Pathways
dependencies.how: Stores the note against the session and the plan.

dependencies.name: Voice-to-Text and AI Documentation
dependencies.how: Turns a dictation into a draft session note for review.

dependencies.name: Zorgverlener Mobile App
dependencies.how: Lets the therapist document a home visit in the mobile app.

steps.title: Record interim measurements and adjust the plan
keyFacts: At the interim moment of the pathway the PROM is offered to the patient in the app and clinical measurements (range of motion, strength, a walking test) are recorded; the score trend is shown in the episode to support the decision to continue, adjust or stop.
Plan adjustments are versioned so that the record shows why the number of sessions changed.
painPoints: Measurements recorded on paper score forms never reach the episode and the outcome series has gaps.

dependencies.name: Measurement Instruments and PROMs
dependencies.how: Offers the PROM and records the clinical measurement at the planned moment.

dependencies.name: Patient Dossier and Care Pathways
dependencies.how: Records the adjustment of the treatment plan with its reason.

steps.title: Run the dossier audit rules before the sessions are declared
keyFacts: Audit rules check the episode for the items an insurer or a Keurmerk visitation looks for: intake present, diagnosis coded, referral data where required, plan with goals, a note per session, measurements at planned moments and an end evaluation when closed.
Sessions of an episode that fails the rules are held back from the declaration batch until the therapist completes the record, which prevents declaring care that the record cannot substantiate.
painPoints: Practices without audit rules discover missing notes during an insurer material audit years later and have to repay declared care.

dependencies.name: Patient Dossier and Care Pathways
dependencies.how: Evaluates the audit rules per episode and lists the missing items.

dependencies.name: Clinical Guidelines and Discipline Templates
dependencies.how: Supplies the audit rule set that fits the discipline, guideline and contract.

dependencies.name: Declaration Engine (GDS801 and Zorgprestatiemodel)
dependencies.how: Holds sessions of incomplete episodes back from the declaration batch.

steps.title: Manage documents and correspondence in the episode
keyFacts: Referral letters, specialist reports, consent forms, photos and outgoing reports are stored in the episode with their origin and date; secure messages received through ZorgMail are filed automatically on the matching patient.
Every access to a document is written to the audit log, which the practice needs under NEN 7510 and to answer a patient's request to know who looked at the record.
painPoints: Documents kept in a shared network folder outside the EPD escape both the retention policy and the audit trail.

dependencies.name: Patient Dossier and Care Pathways
dependencies.how: Files documents and correspondence in the episode.

dependencies.name: Referral and Secure Messaging Hub (ZorgDomein, ZorgMail)
dependencies.how: Files received ZorgMail messages on the matching patient.

dependencies.name: Audit Log, Consent and Information Security
dependencies.how: Logs every document view and download.

steps.title: Close the episode with the end measurement, evaluation and end report
keyFacts: The end measurement completes the PROM series, the evaluation records goal attainment and the reason for closing (goals reached, patient stopped, referred on), and the end report goes to the referrer through ZorgMail or ZorgDomein.

Closing releases the episode for the monthly LDF delivery and marks it for the retention period; the therapist can reopen it when the patient returns for the same complaint within the practice's rules.
painPoints: Episodes left open for months after the last session pollute waiting-time, throughput and outcome statistics.
End reports are skipped when the patient simply stops coming, and the referrer never learns the outcome.

dependencies.name: Patient Dossier and Care Pathways
dependencies.how: Records the evaluation and closing reason and closes the episode.

dependencies.name: Measurement Instruments and PROMs
dependencies.how: Captures the end PROM and clinical measurement.

dependencies.name: Referral and Secure Messaging Hub (ZorgDomein, ZorgMail)
dependencies.how: Sends the end report to the referrer.

streams.name: Measure Outcomes with PROMs and ROM
streams.description: Take a practice or GGZ provider from the choice of a measurement instrument to outcome dashboards and to the quality registers that contracts require. The stream covers PROMs and clinical measurement instruments inside the paramedical treatment, routine outcome monitoring (ROM) for GGZ with questionnaires orchestrated at intake, interim and end, the Embloom library that supplies the questionnaires, benchmarks across therapists and practices, and the monthly pseudonymised delivery to the Landelijke Database Fysiotherapie (LDF), the Keurmerk practice register and other registers under opt-in patient consent. Outcome data is a contract condition for many insurers and the basis for the practice's own quality conversation, so the stream has to make measuring almost free of effort.
outcomes: Patients receive the right questionnaire at the right moment in the app and the score lands in the episode without retyping
Therapists and GGZ practitioners see score trends per patient and per caseload and use them in the treatment conversation
The monthly LDF and Keurmerk delivery is complete, pseudonymised and covered by recorded opt-in consent
Practices can compare their outcomes with the benchmark and answer insurer quality questions from the dashboard

flows.title: From Instrument Choice to Outcome Dashboard in a Paramedical Practice
flows.description: A physiotherapy practice owner configures which PROMs and clinical instruments belong to each care pathway, patients complete them in the app at the planned moments, scores are shown in the episode and aggregated on the practice outcome dashboard, and the practice compares itself with the benchmark ahead of an insurer conversation.
flows.trigger: An insurer contract or the Keurmerk requires outcome measurement, or the owner wants to show treatment results to patients and referrers.
flows.successSignal: Every open episode has start and end measurements planned, the response rate on app questionnaires is visible per therapist, and the outcome dashboard shows the practice against the benchmark.

steps.title: Configure the instruments and measurement moments per care pathway
keyFacts: The owner picks from the instrument library the PROMs (for example PSK and NPRS for musculoskeletal complaints) and clinical tests that each pathway uses, and sets the moments: at intake, at an interim point and at closing.

The LDF minimum data set and the insurer contract conditions define which instruments are mandatory for which diagnosis groups, so the configuration starts from those requirements rather than from personal preference.
painPoints: Therapists in the same practice measure with different instruments, and the practice cannot aggregate its results.

dependencies.name: Measurement Instruments and PROMs
dependencies.how: Binds instruments and moments to the care pathways of the practice.

dependencies.name: Questionnaire and Intervention Library (Embloom)
dependencies.how: Supplies the licensed questionnaires and their scoring rules.

steps.title: Offer the questionnaire to the patient in the app at the planned moment
keyFacts: The pathway triggers the questionnaire before the intake and at the interim and end moments; the patient receives a push notification and fills it on the phone, or on a tablet in the waiting room when the app is not used.
Reminders and a visible 'to do' in the app raise the response rate; the therapist sees in the agenda whether the questionnaire was completed before the consult.
painPoints: Questionnaires sent by e-mail with a generic link are ignored, and the therapist fills the score from memory during the consult.
Elderly patients without the app skip the digital measurement and the practice's outcome data over-represents younger patients.

dependencies.name: Patient App and Web Portal
dependencies.how: Presents the questionnaire and the reminder to the patient in the app.

dependencies.name: Measurement Instruments and PROMs
dependencies.how: Triggers the questionnaire at the planned moment and records the response.

steps.title: Record clinical measurements in the consult
keyFacts: Range of motion, strength, balance, walking or swallowing tests are recorded in structured fields with normal values and previous scores next to them, so that the therapist sees progress at the moment of measuring.
Dietitians and speech therapists use their own instruments (weight and body composition, speech and language tests), configured per discipline in HCI One.
painPoints: Scores written in the free-text note cannot be trended or delivered to a register.

dependencies.name: Measurement Instruments and PROMs
dependencies.how: Stores the clinical measurement with reference values and trend.

dependencies.name: Patient Dossier and Care Pathways
dependencies.how: Places the measurement in the episode next to the plan and notes.

steps.title: Show score trends in the episode and discuss them with the patient
keyFacts: The episode shows the PROM and clinical scores as a trend against the goals, and the therapist shares the trend with the patient in the app, which supports the decision to continue or close and makes progress visible to the patient.
A minimal clinically important difference per instrument is shown so that a change is interpreted correctly.
painPoints: Scores that are collected but never discussed make patients experience questionnaires as administration for the insurer.

streams.name: Declare and Get Paid
streams.description: Take a registered treatment to money on the practice's bank account. The stream covers the insurance eligibility check (COV) through Vecozo before treatment starts, the generation of GDS801 paramedical declarations from the agenda and dossier (GDS801 replaced PM304 on 1 January 2025), zorgprestatiemodel claims for GGZ practices, submission through the Vecozo declaration portal, the handling of return messages with rejection reasons, patient invoices for non-reimbursed care with Mollie payments, the outsourced billing service that handles return messages for practices that prefer not to, and the export to accounting packages such as Twinfield. HCI processed more than 500 million euro in annual declarations at the time of the 2022 investment, so a rejection spike after a standard change is felt immediately in practice cash flow.
outcomes: Declarations are generated from the agenda and dossier without re-registration and submitted to Vecozo in the current GDS801 or zorgprestatiemodel format
Return messages are resolved within the practice or by the billing service before the next batch, so first-time-right rates stay high after standard changes
Patients pay non-reimbursed care and no-show fees online without the practice chasing paper invoices
Every paid claim and invoice is exported to the accounting package with the right ledger allocation

flows.title: From Registered Treatment to an Accepted GDS801 Declaration
flows.description: A physiotherapy practice checks the patient's insurance before the first session, registers treatments through the agenda, generates the GDS801 declaration batch, submits it through Vecozo and processes the return messages until every claim line is accepted or invoiced to the patient.
flows.trigger: A new patient is booked, or the practice's declaration day (weekly or monthly) arrives with registered treatments waiting to be declared.
flows.successSignal: The batch is accepted by Vecozo, the insurer's return message shows the claim lines paid, rejected lines are corrected or invoiced to the patient, and the payment specification is matched to the bank receipt.

steps.title: Check insurance eligibility with COV before the first session
keyFacts: The COV check through Vecozo confirms on BSN and date of birth which insurer and which policy the patient has, and the practice records the result on the patient so that the declaration goes to the right insurer under the right contract.

Physiotherapy for most adults is reimbursed from supplementary insurance with a limited number of sessions per year; the check does not show the remaining sessions, so the practice still discusses the expected coverage with the patient.
painPoints: Patients who changed insurer on 1 January are declared to the old insurer until the practice re-runs the check.
Practices that skip the check for returning patients get rejections on the first batch of the year.

dependencies.name: Patient Dossier and Care Pathways

steps.title: Register treatments through the agenda with the right performance codes
keyFacts: Each completed appointment carries the performance code (for example a regular session, a manual therapy session, a long session, a home visit surcharge) and the diagnosis code from the episode; the therapist confirms the session and the registration is done.

For indications on the chronic list, the sessions that the patient pays first and the sessions covered by the basic insurance are counted per episode so that the declaration route switches at the right session.
painPoints: Therapists who register at the end of the week forget home-visit surcharges and second sessions on the same day.
A wrong diagnosis code on the episode turns every session in it into a rejection.

steps.title: Generate the GDS801 declaration batch and validate it
keyFacts: The declaration engine builds the GDS801 batch per insurer from the registered sessions, validates the mandatory elements (BSN, insurer, performance and diagnosis codes, referral where required, AGB codes of practice and therapist) and the contract rules, and reports the lines that will fail before anything is sent.
GDS801 was developed with PPN, KNGF, ZN, Vektis, Vecozo and EPD vendors and replaced PM304 on 1 January 2025; the engine keeps both formats for corrections of older claims.
painPoints: Practices that send unvalidated batches get the same rejection for every session of a patient and lose a payment cycle.

keyFacts: The batch is submitted through the Vecozo declaration portal with the practice's certificate; the technical acknowledgement and later the insurer's return message are retrieved automatically and matched to the claim lines.
Return messages carry per-line rejection codes (for example patient not insured on the date of treatment, treatment limit exceeded, referral missing) that the practice must interpret.

Practices on the billing service hand this worklist to HCI staff who resolve return messages on their behalf; the practice sees the status but does no rework.
painPoints: Rejection codes are cryptic, and practice owners resubmit the same line unchanged.
Lines that are neither resubmitted nor invoiced to the patient become unnoticed revenue loss.

Youth care and WMO trajectories run on a valid municipal assignment with iJw/iWmo messages exchanged on time

flows.title: From Referral to a Multidisciplinary Treatment Plan
flows.description: A GGZ institution receives a ZorgDomein referral, places the client on the waiting list, runs the intake and diagnostics, types the care demand, sets up the treatment plan with a coordinating practitioner and the involved professionals, and starts registering consults under the zorgprestatiemodel.
flows.trigger: A referral arrives through ZorgDomein or the client contacts the institution directly.
flows.successSignal: The client has an active treatment plan with goals, a coordinating practitioner, the right setting and a registered referral date, and the first consults are registered and declarable.

steps.title: Receive the referral and manage the waiting list
keyFacts: The referral is received through ZorgDomein with the referral date, mandatory on every zorgprestatiemodel declaration from 2026, and the referrer's AGB code that the declaration standard already required; the client is placed on the waiting list for the right team or programme.

Waiting-list status is reported against the Treeknorm (14 weeks from referral to start of treatment); the institution offers the client interim contact, e-health or a consult with another team when the norm is exceeded.
painPoints: Referrals received by fax or as a PDF lack a machine-readable referral date, and the declaration later fails.
Waiting lists kept per team in spreadsheets hide clients who wait longer than the norm.

dependencies.name: Referral and Secure Messaging Hub (ZorgDomein, ZorgMail)
dependencies.how: Receives the referral with referral date and referrer into the client dossier.

dependencies.name: Treatment Plans and Multidisciplinary Coordination
dependencies.how: Registers the client on the CRS waiting list of the right team or programme with the referral date and referrer.

steps.title: Run the intake and diagnostics
keyFacts: Intake consults are registered as diagnostic consults with their setting and profession; the intake questionnaire and ROM baseline are sent before the first appointment through the client portal.
The practitioner documents the intake with SmartAI voice-to-text and records the diagnosis classification and the care-demand typing (zorgvraagtypering) that the model requires.
painPoints: Care-demand typing done weeks after intake as an administrative task rather than a clinical one is unreliable.

dependencies.name: Treatment Plans and Multidisciplinary Coordination
dependencies.how: Stores the intake report, diagnosis classification and care-demand typing on the client's CRS dossier and plan.

dependencies.name: ROM and Questionnaire Orchestration for GGZ
dependencies.how: Sends the intake questionnaires and stores the baseline.

dependencies.name: Voice-to-Text and AI Documentation
dependencies.how: Transcribes and drafts the intake report for review.

steps.title: Set up the treatment plan with the coordinating practitioner and the team
keyFacts: The plan lists goals, the interventions, the involved professionals (psychologist, psychiatrist, nurse, system therapist), the coordinating practitioner (regiebehandelaar) and the planned evaluation moments; the client signs the plan in the portal.
Multidisciplinary meetings are planned and their conclusions recorded against the plan so that every professional works from the same version.
painPoints: Plans that live in a Word document per practitioner diverge from what the team actually does.
Clients who never see their plan cannot take part in decisions about it.

dependencies.name: Treatment Plans and Multidisciplinary Coordination
dependencies.how: Creates the plan with goals, professionals, coordinating practitioner and evaluation moments.

dependencies.name: GGZ Client Portal
dependencies.how: Shows the plan to the client for agreement in the portal.

steps.title: Register consults, settings and group treatment as care is delivered
keyFacts: Each consult is registered from the agenda with type, duration band, setting and profession; group treatment registers one performance per participant, and intercollegial consultation between professionals of different providers has its own performance.
The registration is checked against the plan and the model rules immediately, so the practitioner corrects a wrong setting the same day.
painPoints: Institutions where consults are registered by the secretariat from notes see systematic errors in duration bands.

dependencies.name: Zorgprestatiemodel Registration and Compliance
dependencies.how: Registers consults with setting, profession and duration band and checks them against the model rules.

dependencies.name: Treatment Plans and Multidisciplinary Coordination
dependencies.how: Links each consult to the plan and the professional's role in it.

steps.title: Evaluate the plan with the client and the team
keyFacts: At the planned evaluation moments the ROM results and the goals are reviewed with the client; the plan is adjusted, continued or closed, and the coordinating practitioner records the conclusion.
Evaluation and closing feed the waiting-list and throughput reporting of the institution.
painPoints: Trajectories that are never formally evaluated run on until the client stops coming.

dependencies.name: Treatment Plans and Multidisciplinary Coordination
dependencies.how: Records the evaluation outcome and the plan version.

dependencies.name: ROM and Questionnaire Orchestration for GGZ
dependencies.how: Provides the ROM trend for the evaluation.

steps.title: Log access and enforce professional secrecy within the institution
keyFacts: Only professionals involved in the treatment plan see the dossier; emergency access (break-the-glass) is logged and reviewed by the application manager, and clients can ask who accessed their dossier.
NEN 7510 requires the institution to demonstrate access control and logging on every GGZ dossier.
painPoints: Institution-wide read access for convenience is the most frequent finding in GGZ privacy audits.

dependencies.name: Audit Log, Consent and Information Security
dependencies.how: Logs every dossier access and supports the periodic review of emergency access.

dependencies.name: Treatment Plans and Multidisciplinary Coordination
dependencies.how: Defines who is involved in the treatment and therefore may access the dossier.

flows.title: From Medication and Municipal Assignment to Declared Youth and WMO Care
flows.description: A psychiatrist prescribes and reviews medication inside the CRS dossier, and the institution's application manager runs a youth care trajectory on a municipal assignment: the iJw assignment message, start and stop messages, the monthly declaration message and the handling of municipal responses, in parallel with the zorgprestatiemodel for adult clients.
flows.trigger: A prescriber decides on medication for a client, or a municipality issues or the institution requests an assignment for a youth or WMO client.
flows.successSignal: Medication is prescribed and visible to the client and pharmacy, the municipal assignment is valid for the period and product, start, stop and declaration messages are accepted, and the municipal payments reconcile.

steps.title: Prescribe and record medication in the dossier
keyFacts: The psychiatrist or nurse specialist prescribes from the dossier with the current medication overview and interaction information at hand, and the prescription is sent electronically to the client's pharmacy.
Medication changes are visible to the coordinating practitioner and to the client in the portal, and the client's own medication overview from the pharmacy can be imported for review.
painPoints: Prescriptions written in a separate prescribing system leave the treatment team without a current medication list.

dependencies.name: Medication Management
dependencies.how: Records prescriptions and the medication overview and sends the prescription to the pharmacy.

dependencies.name: GGZ Client Portal
dependencies.how: Shows the client's current medication in the portal.

steps.title: Review medication periodically and record the evaluation
keyFacts: Medication reviews are planned in the treatment plan; the prescriber records effect, side effects and the decision to continue, change or stop, and the review consult is registered as a treatment consult.
Changes trigger an updated medication overview for the client and the pharmacy.
painPoints: Clients on long-term medication without a planned review continue prescriptions for years without an evaluation.

dependencies.name: Medication Management
dependencies.how: Records the review outcome and updates the medication overview.

dependencies.name: Treatment Plans and Multidisciplinary Coordination
dependencies.how: Plans the review moment in the treatment plan.

steps.title: Obtain or request the municipal assignment for youth care or WMO
keyFacts: For clients under the Jeugdwet or WMO the municipality issues an assignment (iJw 301 or iWmo 301) with product code, volume and period, or the institution requests one (315 message); the assignment is stored against the client and the contract with that municipality.
Each municipality or region contracts its own products and tariffs, so the contract register per municipality is the reference for what can be delivered and declared.
painPoints: Care started before the assignment arrives cannot be declared and is written off.
Institutions serving many municipalities lose track of which contract applies to which client.

dependencies.name: Youth Care and Municipal Contracting (Jeugdwet/WMO)
dependencies.how: Stores the municipal assignment and matches it to the municipal contract.

dependencies.name: Patient Dossier and Care Pathways
dependencies.how: Records the municipality as financier on the client's trajectory.

steps.title: Send start and stop messages for the trajectory
keyFacts: The start of care (305 message) and the stop of care (307 message) are sent to the municipality through the standardised exchange when the trajectory starts and ends; the municipality's responses (306, 308) are matched.
Missing start messages are the most common reason a municipality rejects the later declaration.
painPoints: Practitioners do not know that the administration needs a start date until the declaration is rejected.

dependencies.name: Youth Care and Municipal Contracting (Jeugdwet/WMO)
dependencies.how: Generates and tracks start and stop messages and their responses.

dependencies.name: Treatment Plans and Multidisciplinary Coordination
dependencies.how: Signals the start and end of the treatment trajectory.

steps.title: Declare delivered care to the municipality monthly
keyFacts: Delivered care within the assignment is declared monthly (iJw/iWmo 303 declaration message) per municipality; the municipality's response (304) approves or rejects lines, and rejected lines are corrected and resubmitted.
The declaration is checked against the assignment volume and period before sending.
painPoints: Institutions that declare quarterly see cash-flow gaps and lose the correction window on rejected lines.

dependencies.name: Youth Care and Municipal Contracting (Jeugdwet/WMO)
dependencies.how: Builds and sends the declaration message and processes the response.

dependencies.name: Treatment Plans and Multidisciplinary Coordination
dependencies.how: Supplies the delivered care per client and period from the treatment plan and session reports; youth care and WMO support are financed by the municipality, not registered under the zorgprestatiemodel.

steps.title: Reconcile municipal payments and report per contract
keyFacts: Municipal payments are reconciled to declared lines per contract; the manager reports delivered volume against the contract ceiling per municipality to the institution's management.
Audit logging covers who sent which message and who corrected which line, which the municipal audit may ask for.
painPoints: Contract ceilings that are only checked at year end lead to care delivered without payment.

dependencies.name: Youth Care and Municipal Contracting (Jeugdwet/WMO)
dependencies.how: Reconciles payments and tracks volume against the contract ceiling.

dependencies.name: Audit Log, Consent and Information Security
dependencies.how: Records who sent and corrected each message.

externalSystemsThisStreamDependsOn.interface: iJw and iWmo message standards (assignment, start/stop, declaration messages)
externalSystemsThisStreamDependsOn.description: Issue the assignment for youth care (Jeugdwet) or WMO support and receive start, stop and declaration messages through the standardised iJw/iWmo exchange.
Carries the zorgprestatiemodel claims to insurers and the iJw/iWmo messages to municipalities.
Receive prescriptions from the prescriber and provide the current medication overview for medication review.
Send the referral with the referral date that the zorgprestatiemodel declaration requires.

streams.name: Deliver Blended and E-health Care
streams.description: Take a treatment plan and turn it into a blended programme in which sessions in the practice are combined with e-health between sessions. The stream covers the Embloom library of questionnaires and interventions integrated in the EPD, the blended care programme builder that assigns modules and home tasks per client, exercise programmes from partners such as Physitrack for paramedical patients, the Emogy app for behavioural support, video consultation and NICE Connect remote trajectories that have followed patients after discharge since 2014 with Amsterdam UMC, and the monitoring of home tasks by the practitioner. Blended care is how practices and institutions treat more clients with the same professionals and how waiting-list clients receive something before treatment starts.
outcomes: Every client with a treatment plan can receive modules, exercises and questionnaires between sessions from the same dossier
Practitioners see who did what at home and adjust the programme in the next session instead of guessing
Video consultation and remote trajectories replace travel for follow-up without losing the clinical record
Waiting-list clients start with e-health so that the wait is used

flows.title: From Treatment Plan to a Blended GGZ Programme
flows.description: A GGZ practitioner composes a blended programme from Embloom modules and questionnaires for a client with an anxiety disorder, assigns the Emogy app for behavioural support, follows the client's home work between sessions and adjusts the programme at each session, including video sessions when the client cannot come in.
flows.trigger: The treatment plan is agreed and includes e-health, or a waiting-list client is offered a preparatory module.
flows.successSignal: The client has completed the assigned modules and questionnaires, the practitioner has used the progress in the sessions, and the programme is evaluated and closed together with the treatment plan.

steps.title: Select modules and questionnaires from the Embloom library
keyFacts: The library holds 500+ questionnaires and 450 e-health interventions for GGZ, POH-GGZ and somatic care, fully integrated in the EPD; the practitioner filters by problem area, target group and language and previews the module before assigning it.
Institutions can restrict the library to the modules their care programmes endorse and add their own content.
painPoints: Practitioners who do not know the library assign the same two modules to every client.

dependencies.name: Questionnaire and Intervention Library (Embloom)
dependencies.how: Provides the searchable library of interventions and questionnaires with previews.

dependencies.name: Treatment Plans and Multidisciplinary Coordination
dependencies.how: Links the chosen modules to the goals in the treatment plan.

steps.title: Compose the blended programme per client with home tasks
keyFacts: The programme builder sequences modules, questionnaires and home tasks between the planned sessions, sets due dates and decides which parts the client does alone and which are discussed in the session.
Programme templates per care programme speed up composition; the practitioner adjusts them per client.
painPoints: Programmes assigned all at once overwhelm clients, who then stop after the first module.

dependencies.name: Blended Care Programme Builder and Monitoring
dependencies.how: Builds the client's programme with sequence, due dates and session links.

dependencies.name: Questionnaire and Intervention Library (Embloom)
dependencies.how: Delivers the module content into the programme.

steps.title: Assign the Emogy app for behavioural support between sessions
keyFacts: For clients who benefit from cognitive and behavioural support on the phone, the practitioner activates Emogy with exercises and reminders tied to the programme; the client's use is visible in the dossier.
Emogy also serves an autism environment used with NICE Connect trajectories.
painPoints: Apps that are recommended but not connected to the dossier give the practitioner no signal whether they are used.

dependencies.name: Emogy Behavioural Support App
dependencies.how: Activates the app for the client and reports use back to the programme.

dependencies.name: Blended Care Programme Builder and Monitoring
dependencies.how: Places the app tasks in the client's programme.

steps.title: Work through the modules in the client portal
keyFacts: The client logs in once to the CRS client portal or Quli and finds modules, questionnaires, diary and messages in one place; progress is saved per exercise and the practitioner can leave feedback inside the module.
Reminders follow the due dates of the programme.
painPoints: Separate logins for the e-health platform and the portal are the reason clients give for not starting.

dependencies.name: GGZ Client Portal
dependencies.how: Gives the client access to the programme in the portal with one login.

dependencies.name: Blended Care Programme Builder and Monitoring
dependencies.how: Stores progress and feedback per module and task.

steps.title: Monitor progress and adjust the programme in the session
keyFacts: Before each session the practitioner sees what the client did, the questionnaire scores and diary entries, and adjusts the next steps; the session note references the home work.
Clients who stop working on the programme are flagged so that the practitioner can address it early.
painPoints: Practitioners who check progress only when the client mentions it lose the blended effect.

dependencies.name: Blended Care Programme Builder and Monitoring
dependencies.how: Presents progress, inactivity flags and scores per client.

dependencies.name: ROM and Questionnaire Orchestration for GGZ
dependencies.how: Supplies the scores from questionnaires in the programme.

dependencies.name: Treatment Plans and Multidisciplinary Coordination
dependencies.how: Records the CRS session report with reference to the home work done.

steps.title: Hold a video session when the client cannot come in
keyFacts: A video consult is planned in the agenda like any other consult, started from the dossier, and registered as a consult under the zorgprestatiemodel exactly like a face-to-face consult, because the model does not distinguish digital from physical delivery; the client joins from the portal or app without installing software.
The session is documented in the same dossier as face-to-face sessions.
painPoints: Consumer video tools outside the platform breach the institution's security policy and leave no registration.

dependencies.name: Video Consultation and NICE Connect Trajectories
dependencies.how: Runs the video session from the dossier and portal.

dependencies.name: GGZ Client Portal
dependencies.how: Lets the client join the video session from the portal.

flows.title: From Exercise Programme to Remote Follow-up after Discharge
flows.description: A physiotherapist assigns a home exercise programme from a partner app to a patient and follows adherence, and a hospital paramedical coordinator sets up a NICE Connect remote trajectory to follow a patient after discharge with questionnaires, measurements and video contact, as in the Amsterdam UMC premature infant network.
flows.trigger: A treatment plan includes home exercises, or a patient is discharged from the hospital or rehabilitation centre with a need for remote follow-up.
flows.successSignal: The patient does the exercises and reports through the app, the remote trajectory delivers questionnaires and measurements on schedule, deviations reach the coordinator, and the trajectory ends with an evaluation in the record.

steps.title: Assign a home exercise programme from the partner app
keyFacts: From the episode the therapist selects exercises in Physitrack or another connected app; the programme is sent to the patient's app and stored as part of the treatment plan.
The patient receives video instructions and reminders; adherence and pain scores are written back to the episode.
painPoints: Printed exercise sheets are lost, and the therapist does not know whether the patient exercised.

dependencies.name: Exercise Programme Integration
dependencies.how: Creates the programme in the partner app and links it to the episode.

dependencies.name: Patient Dossier and Care Pathways
dependencies.how: Stores the programme reference in the treatment plan.

steps.title: Follow adherence and adjust the exercises
keyFacts: Adherence and reported pain or difficulty per exercise are visible before the next session; the therapist progresses or simplifies the programme and the change is pushed to the patient's app.
The patient sees the programme in the Uw Zorg Online app next to appointments and messages.
painPoints: Patients who use one app for exercises and another for appointments stop using one of them.

dependencies.name: Exercise Programme Integration
dependencies.how: Returns adherence and scores from the partner app to the episode.

dependencies.name: Patient App and Web Portal
dependencies.how: Shows the exercise programme in the patient app.

steps.title: Set up a NICE Connect remote trajectory at discharge
keyFacts: The coordinator chooses the trajectory template (for example follow-up of premature infants in the Amsterdam UMC network, a rehabilitation aftercare trajectory or an autism environment) and sets the schedule of questionnaires, measurements and contact moments for the months after discharge.
The trajectory links the patient's paraNICE record with the hospital information system so that the treating team stays informed.
painPoints: Aftercare organised by phone calls from the outpatient clinic depends on who remembers to call.

dependencies.name: Video Consultation and NICE Connect Trajectories
dependencies.how: Creates the trajectory with its schedule of questionnaires, measurements and contact moments.

dependencies.name: Treatment Plans and Multidisciplinary Coordination
dependencies.how: Records the trajectory as part of the multidisciplinary plan.

steps.title: Collect questionnaires and measurements at home
keyFacts: Parents or patients fill questionnaires and enter measurements (weight, development milestones, function scores) in the app on the schedule; reminders and a clear 'what is next' keep participation high.
Answers outside the expected range raise a signal to the coordinator.
painPoints: Long questionnaires on a phone are abandoned halfway.

dependencies.name: Patient App and Web Portal
dependencies.how: Presents questionnaires and measurement entry to the patient or parent in the app.

dependencies.name: Video Consultation and NICE Connect Trajectories
dependencies.how: Delivers the scheduled items and evaluates the signals.

steps.title: Review signals and hold video contact with the family
keyFacts: The coordinator reviews the signals per trajectory, contacts the family by secure message or a video consult, and involves the treating specialist when needed; contacts are recorded in the trajectory.
Video contact replaces a hospital visit for families who live far from the centre.
painPoints: Signals that go to a shared mailbox are picked up late.

dependencies.name: Video Consultation and NICE Connect Trajectories
dependencies.how: Shows the signals per trajectory and runs the video contact.

dependencies.name: Patient Dossier and Care Pathways
dependencies.how: Records the contact and its conclusion in the patient record.

steps.title: Close the remote trajectory with an evaluation
keyFacts: At the end of the schedule the coordinator evaluates the trajectory, closes it in the record and reports to the treating specialist and the GP; the outcome series is available for the department's reporting.
Trajectories can be extended when the evaluation shows the need.
painPoints: Trajectories without an end date keep sending questionnaires to families who no longer need them.

dependencies.name: Video Consultation and NICE Connect Trajectories
dependencies.how: Closes or extends the trajectory and produces the outcome series.

dependencies.name: Treatment Plans and Multidisciplinary Coordination
dependencies.how: Records the evaluation and closes the trajectory in the plan.

externalSystemsThisStreamDependsOn.interface: Exercise programme APIs and patient apps
externalSystemsThisStreamDependsOn.description: Provide exercise libraries, programme assignment and adherence feedback that the paramedical EPD links to the episode.

externalSystemsThisStreamDependsOn.system: Therapieland, Minddistrict and other e-health platforms
externalSystemsThisStreamDependsOn.description: Alternative e-health content platforms that GGZ institutions may use next to Embloom, with progress written back to CRS.
Carries the video consultation between practitioner and client under the platform's security requirements.

externalSystemsThisStreamDependsOn.system: Apple App Store and Google Play
externalSystemsThisStreamDependsOn.description: Distribute the Emogy and patient apps and deliver reminders for home tasks.

rootGroups.name: Patient and Care Network Journeys
rootGroups.description: From an invitation to an active Uw Zorg Online or client-portal user, from a MedMij consent to a Quli personal health environment shared with family, from a ZorgDomein referral to a report back to the referrer, and from a website template to a findable practice with booking, e-consult and triage entry points: the journeys that make the patient the centre of the care network and reduce phone calls for practices, GPs and pharmacies.

streams.name: Engage Patients through Portal and App
streams.description: Take a patient from an invitation to an active user of the Uw Zorg Online app or the CRS client portal who arranges things digitally instead of by phone. The stream covers activation with DigiD or a practice-issued invitation, e-consult with the GP, pharmacy, therapist or GGZ team, appointment self-service in the practice agenda, repeat prescriptions and the medication overview from the pharmacy system, access to records, treatment plans and correspondence, digital triage such as 'Moet ik naar de dokter?' before contacting the practice, and notifications. Uw Zorg Online connects to the GP and pharmacy information systems (Sanday, HealthConnected, Pharmapartners, CGM) and serves 3 million+ app users, so activation and daily use drive both patient convenience and the reduction of phone calls that practices pay for.
outcomes: A patient invited by a GP practice, pharmacy, therapist or GGZ institution activates the app and finds all their care providers in one place
Routine questions, appointments and repeat prescriptions move from the phone to the app, which the practice sees in fewer calls
Patients read their record, treatment plan and correspondence and receive notifications when something new arrives
Digital triage sends patients to the right route before they contact the practice

flows.title: From Invitation to an Active Uw Zorg Online User
flows.description: A GP practice or pharmacy invites its patients to Uw Zorg Online, the patient installs the app, logs in with DigiD, links the practice, sends a first e-consult and books an appointment, and the practice manager watches activation grow while phone traffic drops.
flows.trigger: The practice enables Uw Zorg Online as its digital front door and invites patients through the website, the waiting room and the phone menu.
flows.successSignal: The patient has an activated account linked to the practice, has used at least one service (e-consult, appointment or repeat prescription), and receives notifications on the phone.

steps.title: Invite patients through the website, waiting room and phone menu
keyFacts: The practice website carries the entry points for the app and the web portal, and the practice uses waiting-room material and the phone menu to point patients to the digital route for routine questions.
The practice manager sees the activation rate per practice and decides which services (e-consult, appointments, repeat prescriptions, record access) to switch on.
painPoints: Practices that switch on the app without telling patients see no reduction in phone calls.

dependencies.name: Practice Websites
dependencies.how: Shows the app and portal entry points and the practice's digital services.

dependencies.name: Patient App and Web Portal
dependencies.how: Lets the practice enable services and see activation.

steps.title: Install the app and log in with DigiD
keyFacts: The patient installs the app from the app store or opens the web portal, logs in with DigiD at the level required for medical data, and the account is created once for all care providers the patient will link.
Family members can be added under their own identity where the care provider allows it.
painPoints: Patients without DigiD or without the DigiD app on their phone drop out at the first login.
Elderly patients need help from the practice or a family member to get through activation.

dependencies.name: Identity, Access and Strong Authentication (UZI/DigiD)
dependencies.how: Authenticates the patient with DigiD and creates or links the account.

dependencies.name: Patient App and Web Portal
dependencies.how: Guides the patient through account creation and first use.

steps.title: Link the practice and see the available services
keyFacts: The patient searches or scans the practice, the link is confirmed against the practice's patient register through the HIS or AIS connector, and the services the practice enabled appear: e-consult, appointments, repeat prescriptions, record.
A patient can link the GP, the pharmacy, the physiotherapist and a GGZ institution and switches between them in the same app.
painPoints: Patients not found in the practice register (a different spelling, a moved patient) cannot link and give up.

dependencies.name: HIS/AIS and Hospital System Connectors
dependencies.how: Verifies the patient in the practice's HIS or AIS and returns the enabled services.

dependencies.name: Patient App and Web Portal
dependencies.how: Links the practice to the patient's account.

steps.title: Send a first e-consult and receive the answer
keyFacts: The patient writes a question, optionally with a photo, and the e-consult lands in the practice's HIS inbox where the GP or assistant answers within the practice's response time; the answer arrives in the app with a notification.
The practice can set e-consult rules (no emergencies, expected response time, which staff answer) that are shown before the patient sends.
painPoints: Practices that answer e-consults in a separate portal instead of the HIS inbox answer late and lose the thread in the record.

dependencies.name: E-consult and Secure Messaging
dependencies.how: Delivers the e-consult to the practice system and the answer back to the app.

dependencies.name: HIS/AIS and Hospital System Connectors
dependencies.how: Passes the e-consult into the HIS or AIS inbox and returns the answer.

steps.title: Book an appointment in the practice agenda from the app
keyFacts: The patient chooses the reason for the visit and picks a slot from the practice's bookable availability; the booking lands in the HIS agenda for a GP or in the paramedical agenda for a therapist, and the confirmation and reminder arrive in the app.
The practice defines which reasons and which slots are bookable online and which require triage or a phone call.
painPoints: Open online booking without a reason for the visit leads to double-length consults booked in single slots.

dependencies.name: Patient Appointment Self-service
dependencies.how: Presents bookable slots by reason and books the appointment.

dependencies.name: Agenda and Multi-location Scheduling
dependencies.how: Provides availability and receives the booking for therapist practices.

dependencies.name: HIS/AIS and Hospital System Connectors
dependencies.how: Provides availability and receives the booking for GP practices.

steps.title: Track activation and the shift from phone to app
keyFacts: The practice manager sees activated patients, e-consults, bookings and repeat requests per month, and uses the view to decide which services to promote next.

Offering the record in the app gives patients the electronic access to their own data that Dutch law expects of care providers; retrieval into the patient's own PGO runs separately under the MedMij framework.
painPoints: Without usage figures the practice cannot tell whether the app is worth the subscription.

dependencies.name: Patient App and Web Portal
dependencies.how: Reports activation and service use per practice.

flows.title: From a Question to the Right Route with Triage, Repeat Prescriptions and Record Access
flows.description: A patient with a new complaint uses digital triage before contacting the practice, orders a repeat prescription from the medication overview, reads the record and correspondence, and a GGZ client uses the CRS client portal for messages with the treatment team, all with notifications that bring the patient back at the right moment.
flows.trigger: The patient has a new complaint, runs out of medication, wants to read a result or letter, or receives a notification from a care provider.
flows.successSignal: The patient reaches the right route (self-care, e-consult, appointment or urgent care), the repeat prescription is ready at the pharmacy, the record is read, and the GGZ client's message is answered by the team.

steps.title: Run digital triage before contacting the practice
keyFacts: The patient answers the triage questions ('Moet ik naar de dokter?') in the app or on the practice website and receives an advice: self-care with instructions, an e-consult, an appointment within a certain time, or urgent contact.
The triage outcome is attached to the e-consult or appointment so that the assistant sees it, and the practice can tune which outcomes lead to which route.
painPoints: Triage that ends with 'call the practice' for every answer adds a step without removing calls.

dependencies.name: Digital Triage
dependencies.how: Runs the triage protocol and produces the advice and route.

dependencies.name: Practice Websites
dependencies.how: Offers the triage entry point on the practice website.

steps.title: Follow the advised route: e-consult or appointment
keyFacts: From the advice the patient starts the e-consult or books the appointment with the triage summary pre-filled, so the practice receives a structured question instead of a phone description.
The advice includes a time frame ('within 24 hours', 'within a week') that maps to the appointment types the practice made bookable, so urgency and slot type match.
painPoints: Patients who get a self-care advice but remain worried call anyway; a follow-up option in the app keeps them in the digital route.

dependencies.name: E-consult and Secure Messaging
dependencies.how: Starts the e-consult with the triage summary.

dependencies.name: Patient Appointment Self-service
dependencies.how: Books the appointment type that matches the advice.

dependencies.name: Digital Triage
dependencies.how: Passes the triage outcome to the chosen route.

steps.title: Order a repeat prescription from the medication overview
keyFacts: The medication overview from the pharmacy information system shows the patient's current medication; the patient selects what to repeat, the request goes to the GP for authorisation and to the pharmacy, and the app tells the patient when it is ready.
The pharmacy manager sees repeat requests arrive in the AIS instead of on the answering machine.
painPoints: Requests for medication that is no longer prescribed create work for the assistant unless the overview is current.

dependencies.name: Repeat Prescriptions and Medication Overview
dependencies.how: Shows the medication overview and routes the repeat request to GP and pharmacy.

dependencies.name: HIS/AIS and Hospital System Connectors
dependencies.how: Reads the medication overview and delivers the request to the pharmacy and GP systems.

steps.title: Read the record, results and letters
