streams.name: Manage Personal Health Data and Sharing
streams.description: Take a citizen from a MedMij consent to a personal health environment (PGO) in Quli or Uw Zorg Online in which health data from the GP, the hospital, the pharmacy and the GGZ institution is retrieved under the MedMij framework, self-measurements and diaries are added, and the person decides who sees what: a partner, a parent, an informal carer or a care professional in the network. Quli carries the MedMij label, offers a GGZ app guide with 50+ apps and single login for e-health, and is used for intensive-care aftercare and by GGZ organisations; HCI won a MedMij PGO tender for Uw Zorg Online. The stream covers consent and data retrieval through DVZA services, self-measurement, granular sharing, network care and the audit trail that makes sharing accountable.
outcomes: A citizen retrieves their own data from connected care providers into one environment under MedMij consent, without asking for printouts
Self-measurements and diaries sit next to professional data and can be shared with the treating professional
Family members and informal carers see exactly what the person allowed, no more, and the person can withdraw it at any time
Care professionals in the network work with the person's environment instead of separate portals

flows.title: From MedMij Consent to a Filled Personal Health Environment
flows.description: A citizen opens Quli or Uw Zorg Online as a PGO, logs in with DigiD, selects the care providers to retrieve data from, gives consent per data service, retrieves the GP record, medication and hospital data, adds self-measurements and a diary, and reviews who has accessed the environment.
flows.trigger: A citizen wants an overview of their own health data across providers, or a care provider suggests a PGO after a diagnosis or treatment.
flows.successSignal: Data from at least one connected provider is retrieved and shown next to self-measurements, consents are recorded and reviewable, and the environment is used as the person's own health overview.

steps.title: Log in with DigiD and choose the PGO environment
keyFacts: The citizen logs in with DigiD at the required level; Quli carries the MedMij PGO label, one of 16 labelled PGOs in November 2025, and the label is what allows it to retrieve data from care providers under the framework; Uw Zorg Online connects through the same MedMij services and HCI won a MedMij PGO tender for it.
The environment explains in plain language what the PGO is, what it can retrieve and that the citizen stays in control.
painPoints: Citizens confuse the care provider's portal with their own PGO and do not understand why data must be retrieved.

dependencies.name: Identity, Access and Strong Authentication (UZI/DigiD)
dependencies.how: Authenticates the citizen at the MedMij assurance level.

dependencies.name: Patient App and Web Portal
dependencies.how: Presents the environment and its explanation after login.

steps.title: Select care providers and give consent per data service
keyFacts: The citizen finds their GP, pharmacy, hospital or GGZ institution in the MedMij participant register and gives consent per data service (for example GP data, medication, lab results); each consent is recorded with date and scope.
Consent can be withdrawn at any time and the withdrawal stops future retrieval; data already retrieved stays in the citizen's environment.
painPoints: Providers that are not yet MedMij-connected (most paramedical practices) cannot be added, which citizens experience as the PGO being incomplete.

dependencies.name: MedMij Data Exchange and Consent
dependencies.how: Looks up connected providers and records consent per data service.

dependencies.name: Audit Log, Consent and Information Security
dependencies.how: Logs the consent and withdrawal events.

steps.title: Retrieve data through the MedMij data services
keyFacts: The PGO retrieves the data from each provider's DVZA service under the consent, maps it to the MedMij information standards and shows it in readable sections: GP journal entries, medication, allergies, lab results, letters, GGZ treatment information.
Retrieval is repeatable, so the environment is refreshed when the citizen asks or on a schedule they set.
painPoints: A retrieval that fails on one provider's side shows an error the citizen cannot act on.

dependencies.name: MedMij Data Exchange and Consent
dependencies.how: Runs the MedMij retrieval per data service and maps the data.

dependencies.name: HIS/AIS and Hospital System Connectors
dependencies.how: Where HCI operates the provider connection, exposes the practice data through the connector.

steps.title: Add self-measurements and a diary
keyFacts: The citizen records blood pressure, weight, mood, pain or activity by hand or from a device and keeps a diary; entries are shown on a timeline next to professional data.
A treating professional can ask the citizen to share a measurement series for a period, for example blood pressure before a GP consult.
painPoints: Measurements kept in a device app that does not connect to the environment stay invisible to the professional.

dependencies.name: Self-measurements and Diaries
dependencies.how: Stores self-measurements and diary entries on the timeline.

dependencies.name: Patient App and Web Portal
dependencies.how: Shows self-measurements next to retrieved professional data.

steps.title: Review who accessed the environment and adjust consents
keyFacts: The citizen sees every retrieval, every share and every access by a family member or professional with date and scope, and adjusts or withdraws consents from the same screen.
The same overview is the basis for a complaint or a question to the care provider, because it shows the legal basis (consent, treatment relationship, emergency) of each access.
painPoints: Access overviews written in technical terms do not tell the citizen who actually looked.

dependencies.name: Audit Log, Consent and Information Security
dependencies.how: Provides the readable access and consent history.

dependencies.name: MedMij Data Exchange and Consent
dependencies.how: Applies consent changes and withdrawals.

flows.title: From a Family Share to Network Care around the Person
flows.description: A GGZ client or a person recovering after intensive care shares parts of the Quli environment with a partner or parent, invites the treating team and an informal carer into a care network, exchanges secure messages and video with the network, and uses the GGZ app guide and single login for e-health apps, while a GGZ institution's application manager rolls Quli out to its teams.
flows.trigger: The person wants a family member or carer to follow their care, or the institution offers Quli as the client environment.
flows.successSignal: The network members see only what was shared, messages and video contact run within the environment, e-health apps open with one login, and the institution's teams work with the client's environment.

steps.title: Share parts of the environment with a partner or parent
keyFacts: The person chooses which sections (agenda, diary, medication, treatment plan, messages) a family member may see and for how long; the family member logs in under their own identity and sees only the shared sections.
Parents of a minor and legal representatives get access according to the rules that apply to the age of the child.
painPoints: All-or-nothing sharing forces the person to choose between privacy and support.

dependencies.name: Network Care and Family Sharing
dependencies.how: Defines and enforces per-section, time-bound sharing with family members.

dependencies.name: Identity, Access and Strong Authentication (UZI/DigiD)
dependencies.how: Authenticates the family member under their own account.

steps.title: Invite the treating team and informal carers into the care network
keyFacts: The person invites the GGZ practitioner, the GP, a district nurse or an informal carer into the network; each member gets a role that defines what they see and whether they can post to the diary or messages.
The institution's practitioners join from the EPD so that the client's environment appears in their worklist.
painPoints: Professionals who must log in to a separate environment per client do not use it.

dependencies.name: Network Care and Family Sharing
dependencies.how: Manages network membership and roles.

dependencies.name: Patient Dossier and Care Pathways
dependencies.how: Links the client's network to the practitioner's dossier and worklist.

steps.title: Message and hold video contact within the network
keyFacts: Secure messaging and video run inside the environment among network members; a message to the practitioner is stored in the dossier and a message between family members stays in the environment.
Reminders for medication, appointments and tasks can be set by the person or, with permission, by a carer.
painPoints: Families that fall back to consumer messaging apps for care coordination lose the link to the professional record.

dependencies.name: E-consult and Secure Messaging
dependencies.how: Carries messages and video among network members.

dependencies.name: Network Care and Family Sharing
dependencies.how: Determines who in the network receives which messages.

steps.title: Open e-health apps from the app guide with one login
keyFacts: The GGZ app guide lists 50+ apps; the person opens an app the practitioner recommends with the environment's single login, and the app's results can be shared back into the environment.
Only apps that passed the platform's security and privacy check appear in the guide, and the practitioner can recommend a specific app from the dossier.
painPoints: Every app with its own account is one more password a client in treatment has to manage.

dependencies.name: Patient App and Web Portal
dependencies.how: Presents the app guide and launches apps with the environment's identity.

dependencies.name: Identity, Access and Strong Authentication (UZI/DigiD)
dependencies.how: Provides the single login token to the connected apps.

steps.title: Use the environment for aftercare after intensive care
keyFacts: After an intensive-care stay the person and their family use the environment for the aftercare programme: information, diary, questionnaires and contact with the aftercare team; the coordinator follows the entries the person shared.
Family members who followed the admission through the shared environment continue in the same place, with the diary and questions collected for the aftercare consult.
painPoints: Aftercare information given on paper at discharge is not consulted at home.

dependencies.name: Self-measurements and Diaries
dependencies.how: Collects the person's entries in the aftercare programme.

dependencies.name: Network Care and Family Sharing
dependencies.how: Gives the aftercare team the access the person granted.

steps.title: Roll out the environment to the institution's teams
keyFacts: The application manager configures which teams offer the environment, which sections are shared from CRS (treatment plan, appointments, messages) and trains practitioners; adoption per team is reported.
Two of the top-50 GGZ organisations used Quli as client portal in 2025, so roll-out material draws on those implementations.

dependencies.name: Network Care and Family Sharing

dependencies.name: Patient Dossier and Care Pathways
dependencies.how: Publishes the shared dossier sections from CRS into the environment.

dependencies.name: Audit Log, Consent and Information Security
dependencies.how: Reports adoption per team and access events for the institution.

streams.name: Refer and Exchange with the Care Network
streams.description: Close the loop between the practice and the rest of the care network: a referral from the GP or specialist through ZorgDomein, secure messaging and reports through ZorgMail, connectors to the GP and pharmacy information systems, hospital information system links for paraNICE in rehabilitation departments, and the report back to the referrer at intake and at the end of treatment. Wegiz (in force April 2023) mandates digital data exchange, and the zorgprestatiemodel and GDS801 declarations depend on referral data, so the exchange is both a care quality and a cash-flow matter.
outcomes: Referrals arrive digitally with referrer, referral date and reason, ready for the dossier and the declaration
Reports to the referrer are generated from the dossier and delivered securely, so GPs know what happened to their patients
Paramedical departments in hospitals work in paraNICE while the hospital information system stays the source of patient identity and orders
Every exchange is traceable and compliant with Wegiz and NEN 7510

flows.title: From ZorgDomein Referral to a Report Back to the Referrer
flows.description: A GP refers a patient to a speech therapist through ZorgDomein, the practice accepts the referral into the dossier and the agenda, treats the patient, sends the intake and end reports through ZorgMail, and the referral data flows into the declaration.
flows.trigger: A referral for the practice appears in ZorgDomein, or a patient hands in a referral letter.
flows.successSignal: The referral is linked to the episode with referrer and referral date, the patient is booked, the reports are delivered and confirmed, and the declaration passes on the referral data.

steps.title: Receive the referral in ZorgDomein and accept it into the practice
keyFacts: The referral carries the referrer's AGB code, the referral date, the reason and the GP's summary; the practice accepts it, and the patient and episode are created or matched in the dossier with those data.
ZorgDomein returns the status (received, accepted, patient contacted) to the GP so that the GP knows the referral landed.
painPoints: Practices that receive ZorgDomein referrals only by e-mail retype the referral data and lose the machine-readable referral date.

dependencies.name: Referral and Secure Messaging Hub (ZorgDomein, ZorgMail)
dependencies.how: Receives and accepts the referral and reports status back.

dependencies.name: Patient Dossier and Care Pathways
dependencies.how: Creates or matches the patient and episode with referrer and referral date.

steps.title: Contact the patient and book the intake
keyFacts: The practice contacts the patient by app message, phone or a booking link and books the intake in the agenda; the waiting time from referral to intake is recorded for the practice's waiting-time reporting.
Patients who already use the Uw Zorg Online app receive the booking link in the app; others are called or e-mailed from the practice's front desk worklist of new referrals.
painPoints: Referrals that wait in the ZorgDomein inbox for days because no one is responsible for them delay the start of care.

dependencies.name: Agenda and Multi-location Scheduling
dependencies.how: Books the intake appointment linked to the referral.

dependencies.name: Referral and Secure Messaging Hub (ZorgDomein, ZorgMail)
dependencies.how: Updates the referral status to 'patient contacted' or 'appointment planned'.

steps.title: Send the intake report through ZorgMail
keyFacts: The intake report is generated from the dossier template of the discipline and sent through ZorgMail to the referrer's HIS, where it files automatically on the patient; the delivery confirmation is stored in the episode.

The report follows the discipline's reporting guideline (for physiotherapy the KNGF guideline on communication with the GP), so the referrer receives the same structure from every practice on the platform.
painPoints: Reports sent as ordinary e-mail attachments breach the AVG and are refused by GPs.

dependencies.name: Referral and Secure Messaging Hub (ZorgDomein, ZorgMail)
dependencies.how: Sends the report and stores the delivery confirmation.

dependencies.name: Patient Dossier and Care Pathways
dependencies.how: Generates the intake report from the dossier.

steps.title: Exchange with the GP during treatment
keyFacts: Questions to the GP (for example about medication or a red flag) and requests for additional referrals or a specialist consultation go through secure messaging; the answers are filed in the episode.
Where the GP's HIS is connected, the patient's relevant GP data can be requested with the patient's consent.
painPoints: Therapists who call the GP practice wait in the phone queue with the patients.

dependencies.name: Referral and Secure Messaging Hub (ZorgDomein, ZorgMail)
dependencies.how: Carries messages between the therapist and the GP.

dependencies.name: HIS/AIS and Hospital System Connectors
dependencies.how: Requests GP data with consent where the HIS is connected.

steps.title: Send the end report and close the referral
keyFacts: At closing the end report with outcome and advice goes to the referrer, and the referral is closed in ZorgDomein; the audit rules check that the report was sent for every referred episode.
The end report includes the outcome measures of the episode so that the GP sees the effect of the treatment, not only that it ended.
painPoints: GPs who never receive an end report cannot judge whether to refer to the same practice again.

dependencies.name: Referral and Secure Messaging Hub (ZorgDomein, ZorgMail)
dependencies.how: Sends the end report and closes the referral.

dependencies.name: Patient Dossier and Care Pathways
dependencies.how: Verifies that the end report is sent before the episode closes.

steps.title: Carry the referral data into the declaration
keyFacts: The referrer's AGB code and the referral date recorded from the referral are used in the GDS801 and zorgprestatiemodel declarations, which from 2026 require the referral date on every claim; a missing referral is flagged before the batch is built.
For directly accessible physiotherapy without a referral the declaration carries the DTF screening instead, and the engine picks the right variant from the episode.
painPoints: Practices that store the referral as a scanned letter only have to type the date into every declaration by hand.

dependencies.name: Declaration Engine (GDS801 and Zorgprestatiemodel)
dependencies.how: Uses the referral data from the episode in the declaration.

dependencies.name: Patient Dossier and Care Pathways
dependencies.how: Holds the referrer and referral date on the episode.

flows.title: From Hospital Order to a Paramedical Record next to the Hospital System
flows.description: A hospital paramedical department receives treatment orders from the hospital information system, registers and records the multidisciplinary treatment in paraNICE, reports back into the hospital record, and exchanges with community practices at discharge, with every exchange logged and the department's connectors managed on the open platform.
flows.trigger: A specialist orders physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy or dietetics for an admitted or outpatient patient, or a patient is discharged with a need for community follow-up.
flows.successSignal: The order is worked in paraNICE with the patient identity from the hospital system, the treatment record and reports are visible in the hospital record, and the discharge handover reaches the community practice.

steps.title: Receive the treatment order and patient identity from the hospital system
keyFacts: The hospital information system remains the source of patient identity, admission and orders; paraNICE receives the order through the connector and creates the paramedical episode with the hospital patient number.
Orders arrive per discipline and are placed in the department's worklist for planning.
painPoints: Departments that re-register patients in their own system create identity mismatches that surface at reporting time.

dependencies.name: HIS/AIS and Hospital System Connectors
dependencies.how: Receives orders and patient identity from the hospital information system.

dependencies.name: Patient Dossier and Care Pathways
dependencies.how: Creates the paramedical episode keyed to the hospital patient number.

steps.title: Plan and coordinate the multidisciplinary treatment
keyFacts: The coordinator assigns therapists per discipline, plans the sessions in the department agenda around the ward schedule, and keeps one treatment plan in which all disciplines record goals and progress for the multidisciplinary meeting.
Ward transfers and discharge dates from the hospital system update the department agenda so that sessions are not planned for a patient who moved or went home.
painPoints: Plans per discipline without a shared view lead to conflicting goals discussed only at the weekly meeting.

dependencies.name: Treatment Plans and Multidisciplinary Coordination
dependencies.how: Holds the shared plan across disciplines.

dependencies.name: Agenda and Multi-location Scheduling
dependencies.how: Plans the sessions per therapist and ward.

steps.title: Record treatment and report into the hospital record
keyFacts: Session notes, measurements and the treatment summary are recorded in paraNICE and a report is sent back into the hospital record through the connector so that the specialist and nurses see the paramedical progress.
paraNICE keeps the detailed paramedical record; the hospital record receives the summary and key measurements, which avoids duplicating the full dossier in two systems.
painPoints: Reports pasted into the hospital record by hand lag days behind the treatment.

dependencies.name: Patient Dossier and Care Pathways
dependencies.how: Stores notes and measurements in the paramedical episode.

dependencies.name: HIS/AIS and Hospital System Connectors
dependencies.how: Sends the paramedical report into the hospital information system.

steps.title: Hand over to community care at discharge
keyFacts: At discharge the department sends a handover report and, where the patient continues in a community practice, a referral through ZorgDomein or a secure message through ZorgMail, and offers a NICE Connect remote trajectory when follow-up is needed.
The handover carries the measurement series and the exercise programme so that the community therapist continues the same instruments and does not restart the baseline.
painPoints: Community practices that receive a discharged patient without a handover start from an empty record.

dependencies.name: Referral and Secure Messaging Hub (ZorgDomein, ZorgMail)
dependencies.how: Sends the handover report and referral to the community practice.

dependencies.name: Treatment Plans and Multidisciplinary Coordination
dependencies.how: Generates the handover from the multidisciplinary plan.

steps.title: Log every exchange for Wegiz and NEN 7510 accountability
keyFacts: Every referral, report and data request is logged with sender, receiver, patient, time and legal basis; the log supports the institution's NEN 7510 audit and the Wegiz requirement to exchange digitally under the applicable information standards.
The log shows the information standard used per exchange, which is what the institution reports when asked how it meets Wegiz for a given exchange type.
painPoints: Exchanges through personal e-mail accounts leave no trace the institution can show an auditor.

dependencies.name: Audit Log, Consent and Information Security
dependencies.how: Logs every exchange with its legal basis.

dependencies.name: Referral and Secure Messaging Hub (ZorgDomein, ZorgMail)
dependencies.how: Emits the events for each referral and message.

Connector changes are versioned like partner interfaces, and the hospital's IT department receives the same change notices as other integration partners.

streams.name: Publish and Run a Practice Website
streams.description: Take a practice from a template to a findable, accessible website that acts as the digital front door: practice websites from the Praktijkinfo portfolio under Uw Zorg Online for GP practices, pharmacies and paramedical practices, with online booking, e-consult, repeat prescription and triage entry points that connect to the practice's agenda and app, content management by practice staff, hosting, security and accessibility. keyFacts: The site goes live with a sitemap and structured data for opening hours and services; the manager updates the practice's business listings so that search results point to the new site and its digital entry points.
Sitemap and structured data are generated from the content model, so opening hours in search results follow the same edit as the website.
painPoints: Old listings that keep pointing to the previous site split the traffic for months.

flows.title: From Daily Updates to a Front Door that Reduces Calls
flows.description: Practice staff keep the website current, publish holiday hours and news, promote the app and its services, watch which entry points patients use, and get support when something breaks, so that the site keeps working as the practice's front door.
flows.trigger: A holiday period, a change in the team or services, a new digital service, or a problem reported by a patient.
flows.successSignal: The site is current, the entry points are used, the practice sees the share of patients arriving through the site, and support cases are resolved.

steps.title: Publish holiday hours, news and team changes
keyFacts: Practice staff update holiday hours, add a news item about a new therapist or a vaccination round, and the change is live immediately without a developer; opening hours also feed the app.
Holiday hours are entered once with a date range and revert automatically, so the site never shows a holiday message in the following week.
painPoints: Staff who need the web agency for every change stop updating the site.

dependencies.name: Practice Websites
dependencies.how: Lets practice staff edit content and hours.

dependencies.name: Patient App and Web Portal
dependencies.how: Shows the same opening hours and news in the patient app.

steps.title: Promote the app and the digital services on the site
keyFacts: The site explains the app, the e-consult rules and the repeat-prescription route, with the activation steps; campaigns such as 'ask your question digitally' are placed on the homepage during busy periods.
The site shows the same service list that the practice enabled in the app, so a patient never sees a service on the site that does not exist in the app.
painPoints: Patients who cannot find how to activate the app call to ask.

dependencies.name: Practice Websites
dependencies.how: Publishes the explanation and activation steps.

dependencies.name: E-consult and Secure Messaging

steps.title: Watch which entry points patients use
keyFacts: The site reports visits and clicks per entry point without tracking cookies, so the manager sees whether triage, booking and e-consult are found and can reorder them.
Usage is compared with the practice's phone volume where the practice records it, which shows whether the front door shifts contact from phone to app.
painPoints: Without usage figures the practice cannot tell whether the triage entry helps or is ignored.

dependencies.name: Practice Websites
dependencies.how: Reports visits and entry-point use in a privacy-friendly way.

dependencies.name: Digital Triage
dependencies.how: Reports how many triage sessions started from the site were completed.

steps.title: Handle a website problem with support
keyFacts: A patient reports that booking does not work; the practice raises a support case, the consultant sees the site, its tenant and the entry-point configuration, and resolves or escalates the issue.
Cases about entry points are routed to the team that owns the booking or triage component, not to the website team, so the fix lands where the problem is.
painPoints: Problems reported to the practice's own IT supplier bounce between parties.

dependencies.name: Customer Support and Onboarding Tooling
dependencies.how: Records and tracks the case with the site context.

dependencies.name: Online Booking, Waiting List and Reminders
dependencies.how: Shows the booking widget configuration and errors for the site.

steps.title: Keep hosting, security and platform updates invisible to the practice
keyFacts: Hosting, certificates, template updates and security patches are applied for all sites on the platform without practice involvement, and the practice is informed only when a change affects its content or entry points.
All practice sites run on the same multi-tenant hosting, so a security patch is applied once for every site instead of per practice.
painPoints: Expired certificates on self-hosted practice sites show browser warnings to patients.

dependencies.name: Multi-tenant Cloud Runtime and Label Migration Tooling
dependencies.how: Applies hosting, certificate and security updates across site tenants.

dependencies.how: Rolls out template improvements to existing sites.

rootGroups.name: Platform and Operations Journeys
rootGroups.description: From a partner agreement to a live connection on the open platform, from a signed practice or an acquired label to live users on HCI One without a forced migration deadline, and from NEN 7510, ISO 27001, AVG, Wegiz and MedMij requirements to audit evidence: the journeys that run the buy-and-build platform behind the labels.

streams.name: Integrate Partners through the Open Platform
streams.description: Take an integration partner from a signed agreement to a live, monitored connection that reaches practices across the HCI labels. Partners include exercise-app vendors (Physitrack, Physiotrack, Fysio AI), questionnaire and quality-register providers (Qualiview, MediQuest), accounting (Twinfield), payments (Mollie), HIS/AIS vendors and clearing houses (Vecozo), and the platform must offer them one onboarding, credentials and consent model, versioned interfaces that behave the same on FysioRoadmap, SpotOnMedics, Incura, CRS and HCI One, sandbox and certification, and monitoring and release coordination so that a change on either side does not break care. The open platform is how HCI adds e-health content and devices without building everything itself.
outcomes: A partner goes from agreement to a certified connection through a documented onboarding with sandbox and test data
One versioned interface serves all labels, so a partner integrates once and reaches 40,000+ professionals
Practice consent and patient consent govern every data exchange with a partner and are visible to the practice
Connection health, volumes and errors are monitored and release changes are coordinated with partners in advance

flows.title: From Partner Agreement to a Certified Connection
flows.description: An exercise-app vendor signs a partner agreement, registers on the developer portal, receives sandbox credentials, builds against the versioned exercise-programme interface, passes the certification tests, and goes live for the practices that enable the partner.
flows.trigger: A partner agreement is signed, or an existing partner needs a connection to an additional label or a new interface version.
flows.successSignal: The partner's connection is certified, listed in the partner catalogue for practices to enable, and the first practices exchange data with it in production.

steps.title: Register on the developer portal and receive sandbox credentials
keyFacts: The partner registers its organisation and technical contacts, accepts the platform terms including the processing agreement required by the AVG, and receives sandbox credentials and test data for the interfaces in scope.
The developer portal documents each interface with versions, scopes and the labels on which it is available.
painPoints: Partners that had a separate connection per acquired label expect to repeat that work for every label.

dependencies.name: Partner API and Open Platform
dependencies.how: Registers the partner, contacts and agreements and issues sandbox credentials.

dependencies.name: Identity, Access and Strong Authentication (UZI/DigiD)
dependencies.how: Issues and manages the partner's client credentials and scopes.

steps.title: Build against the versioned interface in the sandbox
keyFacts: The partner implements the exercise-programme interface: receive a programme request from an episode, return the programme reference, push adherence and scores back; the interface version is fixed at onboarding and supported across labels.
The sandbox mirrors the production behaviour of consent checks so that partners see rejections for missing consent during development.
painPoints: Undocumented label-specific behaviour discovered in production costs partners weeks.

dependencies.name: Partner API and Open Platform
dependencies.how: Runs the sandbox and the versioned interface with test data.

dependencies.name: Exercise Programme Integration
dependencies.how: Defines the programme request, reference and adherence exchange the partner implements.

steps.title: Pass the certification tests for security, consent and data handling
keyFacts: Certification checks authentication, scope use, consent enforcement, error handling, data minimisation and logging; questionnaire partners are also checked on scoring correctness against the library.
The result is recorded with the interface version, and the partner appears in the catalogue that practices can enable.
painPoints: Partners that pass functional tests but log patient data in their own systems fail the security review late.

dependencies.name: Partner API and Open Platform
dependencies.how: Runs and records the certification tests per interface version.

dependencies.name: Questionnaire and Intervention Library (Embloom)
dependencies.how: Verifies questionnaire and scoring conformance for content partners.

dependencies.name: Audit Log, Consent and Information Security
dependencies.how: Records the security and data-handling review outcome.

steps.title: Enable the partner per practice with practice and patient consent
keyFacts: A practice enables the partner from the catalogue, accepts the data exchange description, and the platform issues the practice-scoped credentials; patient-level consent is asked in the app before data flows to the partner.
The practice sees the partner's data exchange description in plain language and can disable the partner at any time, which stops the exchange immediately.
painPoints: Practices that enable a partner without understanding what data leaves the EPD cannot answer patient questions.

dependencies.name: Partner API and Open Platform
dependencies.how: Enables the partner for the practice and issues practice-scoped access.

dependencies.name: Audit Log, Consent and Information Security
dependencies.how: Stores the practice and patient consents for the partner exchange.

steps.title: Go live and monitor the first exchanges
keyFacts: Production credentials are issued, the first exchanges are monitored for errors and latency by both parties, and the partner's support contact is linked to the HCI support tooling for joint incident handling.
Partners with connections to acquired labels are migrated to the platform interface as those labels consolidate into HCI One, on the same schedule as the practices.
painPoints: Errors seen by the practice are reported to HCI, while the cause is on the partner side, and nobody owns the ticket.

dependencies.name: Partner API and Open Platform
dependencies.how: Issues production credentials and monitors exchanges.

dependencies.name: Customer Support and Onboarding Tooling
dependencies.how: Links partner incidents to support cases.

flows.title: From Interface Change to a Coordinated Release across Labels
flows.description: A national standard changes (for example a new declaration specification through Vecozo or a HIS vendor's interface update), the platform team versions the interface, informs partners, runs the change through sandbox and pilot practices on each label, and retires the old version on a published schedule while connection health is monitored.
flows.trigger: A standards body, a national infrastructure party or a partner announces an interface change, or the platform deprecates an interface version.
flows.successSignal: All partners are on the supported version before the retirement date, no practice lost a connection during the change, and the monitoring shows normal volumes and error rates on every label.

steps.title: Assess the change and version the interface
keyFacts: The platform team maps the external change (for example a Vecozo specification update or a HIS connector change) to the affected interfaces and labels, publishes a new interface version with a migration note, and sets the retirement date of the old version.
The GDS801 introduction on 1 January 2025 is the reference case: a national standard change that touched the declaration engine, the Vecozo gateway and partner exports on every label at once.
painPoints: Changes that reach partners through a newsletter instead of the developer portal are missed.

dependencies.name: Partner API and Open Platform
dependencies.how: Publishes the new version, migration note and retirement schedule.

dependencies.name: Vecozo Gateway and Insurance Eligibility
dependencies.how: Supplies the changed Vecozo or national interface behaviour.

steps.title: Inform partners and open the new version in the sandbox
keyFacts: Affected partners receive the change notice with test data and a deadline; their progress against the new version is tracked on the portal.
Partners can test against the new version while the old version stays available in the sandbox, so both can be compared with the same test data.
painPoints: Small partners without a dedicated developer need more lead time than large ones.

dependencies.name: Partner API and Open Platform
dependencies.how: Notifies partners and tracks migration status.

dependencies.name: HIS/AIS and Hospital System Connectors
dependencies.how: Provides the HIS and hospital connector sandbox for the new version.

steps.title: Pilot the change with practices on each label
keyFacts: Pilot practices on FysioRoadmap, SpotOnMedics, Incura, CRS and HCI One run the new version in production with close monitoring; the multi-tenant runtime allows enabling the version per tenant.
Pilot practices are chosen per label and discipline so that the change is seen with each label's data conventions before broad rollout.
painPoints: A change tested on one label only breaks on another label with different data conventions.

dependencies.name: Multi-tenant Cloud Runtime and Label Migration Tooling
dependencies.how: Enables the new version per tenant and label.

dependencies.name: Customer Support and Onboarding Tooling
dependencies.how: Tracks pilot feedback and issues per practice.

steps.title: Roll out to all practices and retire the old version
keyFacts: After the pilot the version is enabled for all tenants, partners still on the old version are contacted, and the old version is retired on the published date with a grace mechanism for critical connections.
Retirement dates are published well in advance and repeated in the portal, so no partner can claim to have been surprised.
painPoints: Retiring a version while one insurer connection still depends on it stops declarations for many practices.

dependencies.name: Partner API and Open Platform
dependencies.how: Enables the version broadly and retires the old one.

dependencies.name: Multi-tenant Cloud Runtime and Label Migration Tooling
dependencies.how: Applies the change across all tenants.

steps.title: Monitor connection health and report to partners and practices
keyFacts: Volumes, error rates and latency per partner, interface and label are monitored; incidents are reported to partners and, where practices are affected, to practices through the support tooling and status page.
Every exchange is logged for audit under NEN 7510.
painPoints: Silent degradation of a partner connection is noticed by practices before the platform team.

dependencies.name: Partner API and Open Platform
dependencies.how: Monitors and alerts on connection health per partner and label.

dependencies.name: Audit Log, Consent and Information Security
dependencies.how: Logs exchanges for audit.

dependencies.name: Customer Support and Onboarding Tooling
dependencies.how: Communicates incidents to practices.

streams.name: Onboard, Migrate and Consolidate Labels
streams.description: Take a newly signed practice, or a practice on an acquired label, to live users on HCI One without disturbing daily care. The stream covers the quote and contract, configuration of agenda, disciplines, care pathways, tariffs and integrations, migration of patients, episodes, documents and open declarations from FysioRoadmap, SpotOnMedics, Incura, Evry, Abakus, Podofile, Edevop or FysioLogic with validation and reconciliation, training, the phased per-discipline rollout with physiotherapy first and no forced migration deadline, hypercare and support. It is the operational heart of the buy-and-build strategy: the promise of 'the best of every label' is only kept if migration is boring.
outcomes: A new practice is configured, trained and live within the agreed onboarding period with declarations flowing from the first month
A practice migrating from an acquired label finds its patients, episodes, documents and open claims complete and reconciled on HCI One
Migration happens per discipline at the practice's pace, with the old label fully supported until the practice chooses to switch
Support and hypercare catch issues in the first weeks and feed them back into the migration tooling

flows.title: From Signed Practice to Live Users
flows.description: A multidisciplinary practice switching from a competitor signs a custom quote, the implementation consultant configures the tenant, disciplines, agenda, pathways, tariffs and integrations, imports the competitor export, trains the team and runs the go-live and hypercare period.
flows.trigger: A practice signs the contract after the custom quote (SpotOnMedics and CRS quote within one business day).
flows.successSignal: The practice runs its agenda, dossier and declarations on the platform, the first declaration batch is accepted, users are trained, and the hypercare period ends with open issues resolved.

steps.title: Confirm the quote and plan the onboarding
keyFacts: The quote is based on number of therapists, disciplines, modules and integrations; the onboarding plan sets the go-live date, the data-migration source, the training schedule and the responsible person at the practice.
The practice's Vecozo certificate, AGB codes and insurer contracts are collected so that declarations work from day one.
painPoints: Go-live dates set around insurer contract renewals or the year change collide with the practice's busiest administrative weeks.

dependencies.name: Customer Support and Onboarding Tooling
dependencies.how: Creates the onboarding case with milestones and responsibilities.

dependencies.name: Multi-tenant Cloud Runtime and Label Migration Tooling
dependencies.how: Provisions the practice tenant with its label and modules.

steps.title: Configure disciplines, agenda, care pathways, tariffs and integrations
keyFacts: The consultant configures therapists and locations, working hours and appointment types, the disciplines with their templates and pathways (KNGF, NVLF, NVD based), insurer contracts and tariffs, patient-invoice tariffs and the integrations the practice uses (Vecozo, Mollie, Twinfield, exercise app, ZorgMail).
Configuration is done from templates per practice type so that a standard practice needs few manual settings.
painPoints: Practices that copy every setting from the old system carry their old workarounds into the new one.

dependencies.name: Agenda and Multi-location Scheduling
dependencies.how: Sets up therapists, locations, hours and appointment types.

dependencies.name: Clinical Guidelines and Discipline Templates
dependencies.how: Activates the templates and pathways per discipline.

dependencies.name: Declaration Engine (GDS801 and Zorgprestatiemodel)
dependencies.how: Loads insurer contracts and tariffs.

dependencies.name: Partner API and Open Platform
dependencies.how: Enables the practice's partner integrations.

steps.title: Import and validate the export from the previous system
keyFacts: Patients, open episodes, documents and open declarations are imported from the competitor's export; the migration tooling validates BSN, insurer and referral data and reports records that need attention before go-live.
Closed episodes are imported for the retention duty and marked read-only.
painPoints: Exports from competitor systems lack documents or measurement data, and the practice keeps the old system for lookups.

dependencies.name: Multi-tenant Cloud Runtime and Label Migration Tooling
dependencies.how: Imports, validates and reports the migrated data.

dependencies.name: Patient Dossier and Care Pathways
dependencies.how: Receives the patients, episodes and documents.

steps.title: Create users and train the team by role
keyFacts: Users are created with their roles (therapist, front desk, owner, billing) and strong authentication; training is role-based and delivered on-site or online before go-live with the practice's own data.
Training uses the practice's own migrated data, so therapists learn on their real patients and pathways rather than a demo practice.
painPoints: Front-desk staff trained on the therapist workflow do not learn the online-booking and waiting-list settings they actually manage.

dependencies.name: Identity, Access and Strong Authentication (UZI/DigiD)
dependencies.how: Creates users with roles and strong authentication.

dependencies.name: Customer Support and Onboarding Tooling
dependencies.how: Schedules and tracks training completion per user.

dependencies.name: Online Booking, Waiting List and Reminders
dependencies.how: Configures online-booking and reminder rules with the front desk.

steps.title: Go live and run the first declaration batch
keyFacts: On go-live day the agenda runs on the new system, the consultant is on standby, and the first declaration batch is generated and submitted through Vecozo under close watch so that any configuration error surfaces on the first return message.
The first batch is deliberately small and submitted early in the week so that the return message arrives while the consultant is still on standby.
painPoints: A wrong AGB code in the configuration rejects the whole first batch and shakes the practice's confidence.

dependencies.name: Declaration Engine (GDS801 and Zorgprestatiemodel)
dependencies.how: Generates and submits the first declaration batch.

dependencies.name: Customer Support and Onboarding Tooling
dependencies.how: Tracks go-live issues in real time.

steps.title: Run hypercare and hand over to regular support
keyFacts: During hypercare all questions go to the onboarding consultant, issues are resolved or logged, and after the agreed period the practice is handed over to regular support with the onboarding case closed and adoption figures (online booking, app activation, declaration acceptance) reviewed with the owner.
Issues found in hypercare that stem from configuration templates are fed back so that the next practice of the same type does not hit them.
painPoints: Practices that never learn where to find help after hypercare go back to phone calls to the consultant.

dependencies.name: Customer Support and Onboarding Tooling
dependencies.how: Runs hypercare and closes the onboarding case.

dependencies.name: Practice BI Dashboards and Reporting
dependencies.how: Shows adoption figures for the handover review.

flows.title: From an Acquired Label to HCI One per Discipline
flows.description: A practice on an acquired label (for example Incura with physiotherapy and dietetics) migrates to HCI One in phases: physiotherapy first as the platform supports it, dietetics when Evry-based dietetics is live on HCI One, with the old label fully supported in between, data migrated and reconciled per phase, and no forced deadline.
flows.trigger: HCI One supports the practice's discipline and the practice decides to migrate, or the practice asks for a migration plan.
flows.successSignal: Each discipline is migrated with complete, reconciled data and trained users, the practice works on HCI One for the migrated disciplines and on the old label for the rest, and the old label is decommissioned for the practice only when the last discipline has moved.

steps.title: Assess the practice and choose the migration phases
keyFacts: The assessment lists disciplines, integrations, custom pathways and reports the practice uses on the old label, and maps them to HCI One; disciplines not yet supported stay on the old label, and the practice sets its own pace.

HCI One is built on the web-based FysioRoadmap foundation and consolidates FysioRoadmap, SpotOnMedics, Incura, Evry, Abakus, Podofile, Edevop and FysioLogic, rolled out per discipline with physiotherapy first.
painPoints: Practices fear losing label-specific features they rely on, and an assessment that hides gaps breaks trust at go-live.

dependencies.name: Customer Support and Onboarding Tooling
dependencies.how: Records the assessment and the phased plan with the practice.

dependencies.name: Multi-tenant Cloud Runtime and Label Migration Tooling
dependencies.how: Maps old-label configuration to HCI One capabilities per discipline.

steps.title: Run a trial migration and reconcile counts and samples
keyFacts: The migration tooling migrates the discipline's patients, episodes, notes, measurements, documents, agenda and open declarations to a trial tenant; counts per entity and sampled episodes are reconciled with the old label, and mapping issues are fixed before the real run.
The reconciliation report is shared with the practice owner, who signs off the sampled episodes before the final migration is planned.
painPoints: Measurement series and pathway steps that map to different structures lose their history if the mapping is not checked on real episodes.

dependencies.name: Multi-tenant Cloud Runtime and Label Migration Tooling
dependencies.how: Runs the trial migration and produces reconciliation reports.

dependencies.name: Patient Dossier and Care Pathways
dependencies.how: Receives the migrated episodes for sample checks.

steps.title: Configure HCI One for the discipline and train its therapists
keyFacts: The discipline's pathways, templates, tariffs and integrations are configured on HCI One, users of that discipline get access, and training focuses on what changed compared with the old label.
Integrations already active on the old label (exercise app, ZorgMail, Twinfield) are re-enabled on HCI One through the partner platform so the practice keeps its partners.
painPoints: Therapists who work in both systems during the transition mix up which agenda to use.

dependencies.name: Clinical Guidelines and Discipline Templates
dependencies.how: Configures pathways and templates for the migrated discipline.

dependencies.name: Identity, Access and Strong Authentication (UZI/DigiD)
dependencies.how: Grants HCI One access to the discipline's users.

dependencies.name: Agenda and Multi-location Scheduling
dependencies.how: Runs the migrated discipline's agenda on HCI One next to the old label.

steps.title: Cut over the discipline with a final migration and open-claim handover
keyFacts: The final migration runs over a weekend, open declarations and return messages are handed over so that no claim is declared twice or lost, and the discipline's users start on HCI One on Monday with the consultant on standby.
The old label is set read-only for the migrated discipline so that therapists cannot record in two places by mistake.
painPoints: Declarations submitted from the old label whose return messages arrive after cut-over are not seen in the new system unless handed over.

dependencies.name: Multi-tenant Cloud Runtime and Label Migration Tooling
dependencies.how: Runs the final migration and freezes the discipline on the old label.

dependencies.name: Declaration Engine (GDS801 and Zorgprestatiemodel)
dependencies.how: Transfers open declarations and pending return messages.

steps.title: Support the practice on both systems during the transition
keyFacts: Support cases are tagged per system, the old label keeps receiving updates for regulation changes such as GDS801, and the practice's dashboard combines figures from both systems during the transition.
There is no forced migration deadline; the practice decides when the next discipline moves, and support capacity is planned per label accordingly.
painPoints: Practices that feel pushed to migrate before their discipline is ready leave for a competitor.

dependencies.name: Customer Support and Onboarding Tooling
dependencies.how: Handles cases across the old label and HCI One.

dependencies.name: Practice BI Dashboards and Reporting
dependencies.how: Combines practice figures from both systems.

steps.title: Decommission the old label for the practice after the last discipline
keyFacts: When the last discipline has moved, the practice's data on the old label is archived under the retention duty, access is closed, and the practice's integrations and certificates are confirmed on HCI One; the practice's feedback feeds the migration tooling for the next practice.
Archived data can be retrieved through a support case for an insurer material audit or a patient request during the retention period.
painPoints: Archived data that cannot be retrieved for an insurer audit years later is a liability for the practice.

dependencies.name: Multi-tenant Cloud Runtime and Label Migration Tooling
dependencies.how: Archives the old-label tenant and closes access.

dependencies.name: Customer Support and Onboarding Tooling
dependencies.how: Closes the migration case and records feedback.

streams.name: Secure and Comply with Health Information Standards
streams.description: Turn the regulation that applies to a healthcare software provider into controls and evidence: NEN 7510 and ISO 27001 information security management, AVG consent, retention and data-subject rights, audit logs on every dossier access, UZI and DigiD authentication for professionals and citizens, Wegiz and MedMij conformance for data exchange, secure development and release, and incident and data-breach response. HCI is certified for NEN 7510 and ISO 27001 and operates from the Netherlands and Switzerland; the stream is what keeps those certificates and what every insurer, institution and hospital asks for before contracting.
outcomes: The NEN 7510 and ISO 27001 certificates are maintained with evidence collected from the platform rather than assembled by hand before the audit
Every access to patient data is authenticated at the right level and logged, and patients and institutions can see who accessed what
Consent, retention and data-subject requests are handled within the AVG deadlines from the platform
Incidents and data breaches are detected, contained, reported and learned from within the legal time limits

flows.title: From Controls to Audit Evidence for NEN 7510 and ISO 27001
flows.description: HCI's security officer and implementation staff maintain the control set, collect evidence from identity, audit-log, runtime and consent systems, run access reviews and supplier assessments, handle the certification audit and follow up findings, while institutions' application managers run their own access reviews and receive the assurance they need for their own NEN 7510 obligations.
flows.trigger: The annual audit cycle, a new institution's supplier assessment, or a change in the platform or the standards.
flows.successSignal: The audit closes with the certificates maintained, findings have owners and dates, and institutions have the supplier assurance documents they asked for.

steps.title: Maintain the control set and the risk register
keyFacts: Controls from NEN 7510 and ISO 27001 are mapped to platform components and owners; the risk register is updated for changes such as a new label migration, a new partner interface or an AI documentation feature.
HCI operates in the Netherlands and Switzerland, so the control set covers both locations and the data residency requirements of Dutch healthcare customers.
painPoints: A control set kept in documents diverges from what the platform actually enforces.

dependencies.name: Audit Log, Consent and Information Security
dependencies.how: Holds the control set, owners and evidence sources.

dependencies.name: Multi-tenant Cloud Runtime and Label Migration Tooling
dependencies.how: Supplies the component and tenant inventory the controls apply to.

steps.title: Enforce strong authentication and run periodic access reviews
keyFacts: Professionals authenticate with strong authentication (UZI where required, otherwise multi-factor), citizens with DigiD; roles follow the involvement in treatment, and quarterly access reviews confirm that leavers and role changes are processed.
Practices with staff turnover receive the review list from the platform so that the practice owner, as controller, confirms who should still have access.
painPoints: Shared front-desk logins defeat the audit trail and are a recurring audit finding.

dependencies.name: Identity, Access and Strong Authentication (UZI/DigiD)
dependencies.how: Enforces strong authentication and role assignment.

dependencies.name: Audit Log, Consent and Information Security
dependencies.how: Produces the access review lists and records the outcome.

steps.title: Collect audit-log evidence and review dossier access
keyFacts: Every dossier access, export and data exchange is logged; the application manager reviews break-the-glass access and unusual patterns monthly and answers patient requests to know who accessed their record.
Logs are retained for the period the institution's policy and NEN 7510 require and are exportable per patient for a request.
painPoints: Logs that cannot be searched per patient make the patient's access request a manual effort.

dependencies.name: Audit Log, Consent and Information Security
dependencies.how: Provides searchable logs and review workflows.

dependencies.name: Patient Dossier and Care Pathways
dependencies.how: Emits access events for every dossier action.

steps.title: Assess suppliers and data-exchange conformance
keyFacts: Hosting and sub-processors are assessed, and the exchange channels (Vecozo certificates, ZorgDomein and ZorgMail connections, MedMij qualification of the PGO and DVZA services) are kept in conformance with their renewal and re-qualification requirements.
Renewal dates for certificates and qualifications are tracked centrally with reminders to the owners well before expiry.
painPoints: A lapsed MedMij qualification or Vecozo certificate stops a service for every practice at once.

flows.title: From Consent and Retention to Incident Response
flows.description: The platform handles AVG consent and data-subject requests, applies retention and archiving per record type, monitors for security events across tenants, and when a data breach occurs, contains it, informs the affected practices and institutions, and reports to the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens within the legal time limit.
flows.trigger: A patient exercises a right, a retention period expires, a security alert fires, or a practice reports a suspected breach.
flows.successSignal: Requests are answered within the AVG deadlines, retention runs without losing records under a legal hold, and incidents are contained, reported where required and closed with lessons applied.

steps.title: Record consent at the right moments and make it visible
keyFacts: Consent for quality-register delivery, for exchange with a partner app, for MedMij retrieval and for family sharing is asked in context and stored with scope and date; the patient sees and changes consents in the app.
The consent record names the purpose and the receiving party so that a practice can show exactly which consent covered an exchange.
painPoints: One general consent form at intake does not cover later exchanges, and practices cannot prove the specific consent.

steps.title: Handle access, correction and deletion requests
keyFacts: A patient's request to access, correct or delete data is logged as a case, the practice is the controller and decides, and the platform produces the export or applies the correction; medical records are subject to the WGBO retention duty, so deletion requests are weighed against it.
Requests and their deadlines are visible to the practice as controller and to HCI as processor, so both see when the one-month AVG period is running out.
painPoints: Requests sent to HCI as processor stall when the practice as controller is not involved.

steps.title: Apply retention and archiving per record type
keyFacts: Retention periods per record type (medical record under the WGBO, financial records, logs, messages) are applied per tenant; records under a legal hold or an open claim are excluded, and archived data remains retrievable for audits.
Practices can set a longer retention where their professional standard requires it, but never shorter than the legal minimum.
painPoints: Practices that never archive keep every record forever, which the AVG does not allow.

steps.title: Detect and contain a security incident
keyFacts: Security monitoring across the multi-tenant runtime raises alerts on unusual access, failed authentications and data exports; the incident team contains the incident, determines which tenants and patients are affected, and preserves the logs.
Containment actions such as revoking credentials or isolating a tenant are logged with time and actor for the later report.
painPoints: Incidents reported by a practice's therapist by phone reach the incident team hours late.

steps.title: Inform affected practices and report to the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens
keyFacts: Affected practices and institutions are informed through secure messaging with the facts they need as controllers; where the breach must be reported, the report goes to the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens within 72 hours, and patients are informed when the risk requires it.
The notification tells the practice whether it must inform its own patients and offers a template, because the practice, not HCI, is the controller.
